items.body: In musical notation, al niente means “to nothing”: a gradual fading until sound disappears. The title suits this debut by Beatrice Miniaci, Cosimo Fiaschi, Gabriele Pagliano and Luca Venitucci, a quartet whose music is shaped by subtraction. Three collective improvisations sit alongside compositions by Stefan Thut and Pagliano, with gestures pared down to small fluctuations of breath, timbre and silence. The four musicians rarely behave as separate voices. In the accompanying interview, they describe coming to think of the ensemble as “one instrument instead of the sum of four different voices”, an approach that can be heard throughout the record. Flute, soprano saxophone, accordion and double bass converge into shifting composite timbres, occasionally separating long enough for an individual instrumental character to surface before being absorbed again. Stefan Thut’s “Some, 1–4” uses an extremely limited vocabulary of sound and noise to produce a surprisingly fluid landscape. Small differences in duration and articulation create movement within a score that otherwise appears almost static. Pagliano’s “Umbra” is similarly economical, tracing the relationship between a gesture and its “shadow” through minute changes in resonance. Extended techniques belong to the music’s basic vocabulary: pitch gives way to breath, friction and resonance, while instrumental identities become increasingly uncertain. Silence has an active role throughout. Venitucci describes it as a continuous field from which individual sounds acquire their presence, and the album makes that relationship unusually tangible. An attack or breath changes the space around it; a resonance continues to register as it approaches inaudibility. In the closing minutes of the final improvisation, the double bass briefly emerges on its own before the other instruments return and the music slowly thins away, approaching the niente of the title. AL NIENTE – photo by Alessandro Carpentieri To guide us towards silence, we reached out directly to Cosimo Fiaschi, Beatrice Miniaci, Gabriele Pagliano, and Luca Venitucci. Listening to al niente, I often lost track of where one instrument ended and another began. The quartet continually reshapes itself into a single, evolving timbre before individual voices briefly re-emerge. Even in the collective improvisations, there’s very little sense of anyone stepping forward as a soloist. Is that something you consciously cultivate, or does it simply emerge from the way each of you listens and responds to the others? The ensamble: Reducing the material down to its bare bones often implies unison, where one instrument is the continuation of the other. In a way, it felt natural to investigate the unison of four very different instruments, that do not share any (?) musical literature. Probably the idea of soloist ceased to be valid while working primarily with long tones and silences. In both improvisations and repertoire, it seems way more interesting to think of the quartet as one instrument instead of the sum of four different voices. The music we made deals with few musical parameters in which details plays a crucial role: but a sharp attack or a little crescendo, for example, could also be the sings of a more prominent musical action which could be understand as some sort of soloist role. In the last track of the album, at approximately six minutes the double-bass introduces the final with a brief solo. That action, for instance, could be understood as a soloist role, since it’s the only one with articulation, in the sense of density. Stefan Thut describes “Some, 1–4” as a score in which the notated image seems to liquefy when it is brought into sound, only to return repeatedly to its original static form. Listening to the piece, I had the impression that the music was constantly oscillating between movement and stillness, almost as if the score itself were breathing. As performers, how did you approach that balance? Did the notation leave room for individual interpretation, or did it require a very precise collective discipline? The ensamble: First of all, we really have to thank Stefan Thut for his availability and for agreeing to share his work with us. The piece consists of four combinations of the letters x and y, where x is sound and y is noise. We choose this piece for its simplicity within the relation sound / noise, as well as the interest in contingencies, since the individual sound and noise (one for every musician in both categories) are chosen a priori. The piece needs an individual discipline since each performer chooses only one of the four permutation (that is also chosen a priori): sound / sound; sound / noise; noise / sound; noise / noise. The oscillation between movement ad stillness you were referring to is generated through the different durations that each of us gave to each sound / noise. In this sense, it’s amazing how a very limited material (six different musical objects within four performers) can create such movements. Both the flute and the soprano saxophone seem to occupy a particularly unstable position on the album. At various moments they cease to function as melodic instruments and instead become sources of breath, friction, multiphonics and noise, often blurring the distinction between pitched sound and pure timbre. How has your relationship with your instruments changed through working with al niente? Has this ensemble altered the way you think about tone production itself? Beatrice Miniaci and Cosimo Fiaschi: The constellation of al niente (four acoustic instruments without resonances) is the perfect setting to let the subtle characteristics of the flute, bass flute and soprano saxophone emerge through the techniques you mentioned. The air quality is a particular trait d’union between the overall ensemble: the accordion is an aerophone too and the double-bass with the archetto is capable of producing many air sounds. Generally speaking, the overall dryness of the quartet in the discreet dynamics is the ideal setting to dig into the liminal zone between air and pitch for our instruments. Pagliano, in your notes on “Umbra”, you describe the relationship between a sound and its “shadow”, referring to positive and negative sounds almost as if they were photographic images. Listening to the piece, I was struck by the fact that these shadows never feel electronic or artificial; they seem to emerge naturally from the instruments themselves. When composing “Umbra”, were you thinking primarily in terms of acoustics and resonance, or was the idea of the “shadow” also a way of exploring the relationship between action, memory and listening? Gabriele Pagliano: Thank you for you deep listening. The core of this piece can be find in the gesture, or action, as a musical object. Every possible reflection about resonance or acoustic spectrum originates from there: the possibilities that come from the process of transformation, or permutation of a single or composed gesture. Even if the sonic texture has to take a central role in the performer thinking, the compositional approach revolves around this idea more than a spectralist approach in a narrow sense. In this perspective, the fact that we never feel these shadow parts “artificial” it’s a welcomed consequence; I think that the realm of the acoustic instruments it’s were the borders between sound and silence are the closest possible and in this sense the gesture is the device that naturally activates that relationship. Venitucci, with more than three decades of experience in experimental music, you’ve worked in contexts ranging from free improvisation to contemporary composition. What fascinates me about al niente is its refusal to treat quietness as simply the absence of sound. Silence often feels active, almost as if it were another performer shaping the music. Has your understanding of silence changed over the years, and what does this ensemble allow you to explore that other improvising groups perhaps do not? Luca Venitucci: My early approach to sound was shaped by rock and European improvised music of the 1960s and 1970s, and naturally tended towards rather assertive gestures. Later, through Ensemble Zeitkratzer, I came into contact with the Wandelweiser movement and Berlin’s Echtzeitmusik scene, which led me to develop a deeper awareness of silence, not as a mere absence of sound, but as a continuous field from which each sonic event emerges and takes on depth and presence. In al niente, this focus on silence brings the finest qualities of sound into the foreground, revealing the subtle transformations and inflections that arise from each musician’s intentions and from their interaction. (Gianmarco Del Re)
items._cn_summary: 这是意大利四人组合 al niente 的同名首张专辑，以「减法」为核心创作哲学。乐评详细解读了团名含义——音乐术语中「渐弱至无声」之意，精准对应了整张专辑的美学取向。长笛、高音萨克斯、手风琴与低音提琴四种本不相近的乐器，通过极简素材、呼吸、摩擦与共振等扩展技巧，融合为一个不断变化的复合音色体，乐手间几乎消解了独奏与伴奏的边界。专辑包含三段集体即兴以及 Stefan Thut 与 Pagliano 的作曲作品，其中 Thut 的「Some, 1–4」以极有限的乐句库构建出流动的声景，Pagliano 的「Umbra」则探讨音响与其「阴影」之间的关系。沉默被视作声音从中浮现的连续场域，而非空缺。最终曲末尾低音提琴短暂独现后，乐队重新汇聚并缓缓消隐，呼应了标题所指的「niente」。

items.body: What makes Headphone Beats 2025-2026 so exciting is that it never settles into its own language. Every time you think you’ve identified the rules, it quietly moves the goalposts. Genres are treated less as destinations than as raw materials: broken apart, stretched, folded, obscured and rebuilt into strange new functional objects. Moments of tenderness appear inside the delicate violence Headphone Beats 2025-2026 by Winter Back   South Korea’s Wona returns in a different spacesuit with Headphone Beats 2025-2026 by Winter Back, an album that feels less like a collection of tracks than a future archetype: a visceral, crystal-clear demonstration of what electronic sound work can become when technique, instinct and design aesthetics are allowed to mutate together. I’d hazard a guess it was made through a pair of headphones over the course of a year, because there’s something intensely close-up about it—and the title proposed, eh? On the surface, you might identify glitch aesthetics, but that’s only the doorway. Beneath it are drill and trap rhythms, tensile funk, lo-fi breakbeat trippery, obfuscation, drops, crescendos, proto-brass, rolling bass and complex and simple synthesis that seems perpetually on the verge of becoming something else. I’m genuinely thrilled this landed on my figurative desk. It’s remorselessly stunning. “Matmat” has my heart: thunderous, rolling beats tumble around each other in waterfalls of hugeness and electrification while the low end holds you prisoner. “AGN” stinks—in the very best sense. Its half-time stutter is a screwface anthem of dropping beat and bass pulse, scratch-and-tear music so filthy you can almost smell it. Backward melodies emerge from the darkness to lighten the load, moments of tenderness appearing inside the delicate violence. “There is beauty in the abrasion and an almost ridiculous confidence in allowing sounds to seem to remain unresolved.” ~Will Wonks And this is the crucial distinction: this isn’t impenetrable sound design made to impress other sound designers. It’s a highly informed, deeply nuanced deviance in sound, rhythm and strata. Our title track “Winter Back” demonstrates an enviable approach to drum programming before its apparent mid-point collapse detonates into a spanking groove of epic proportions—the holy grail of contemporary electronic funk. “TLD” may contain the most outrageous break on the record, somehow folding rhythm back into itself and emerging as something entirely new: a funky drummer for 3026. Nearly every track appears to reach a point where it dissolves, sheds its skin and reconstitutes somewhere else. These aren’t conventional breakdowns so much as dimensional ruptures. “Bedrop” is the perfect example: atmosphere and tense pads briefly suspend the album in mid-air before the future-klaxon begins its nagging ascent and the whole thing lurches forward again. “Set Jen” brings tribal toms and deranged circus bells into some kind of beautifully unstable agreement. “Dedication” removes the floor entirely, a beatless blast of aural oxygen that makes the subsequent savagery hit harder. “Starb” and “Still Ago” sound like saucepans being thrown down the stairs through a malfunctioning computer, grinding the listener into submission, before “220” closes the circuit with single hi-hits, elastic wubs and a sense of space suddenly expanding beyond the edges of the record. What makes Headphone Beats 2025-2026 so exciting is that it never settles into its own language. Every time you think you’ve identified the rules, it quietly moves the goalposts. Genres are treated less as destinations than as raw materials: broken apart, stretched, folded, obscured and rebuilt into strange new functional objects. There is beauty in the abrasion and an almost ridiculous confidence in allowing sounds to seem to remain unresolved. It feels experimental without announcing itself as experimental. It feels futuristic without resorting to the usual sci-fi vocabulary. Most importantly, it feels alive. It’s a great example of electronic music one would want to spend time inside, not simply consume. The deeper you go, the more its internal architecture reveals itself: tiny rhythmic decisions, concealed transitions, unexpected pockets of funk, bass frequencies that seem to have their own gravitational field. It rewards repeated listening because it keeps changing shape under examination. You don’t exhaust it; you develop a better understanding of how much is actually happening. A genuinely extraordinary piece of work. A 10/10 proposition where nothing is missing and nothing needs adding. Rare. Welcomed. Headphone Beats 2025-2026 is available on SoundSupply_Service. [Bandcamp] Headphone Beats 2025-2026 by Winter BackThe post Winter Back :: Headphone Beats 2025-2026 (SoundSupply_Service) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以电子声音设计为核心，将glitch美学作为入口，深入到drill、trap、lo-fi breakbeat、funk等多种节奏语言的拆解与重组中。每首曲目似乎都到达某个临界点后瓦解、蜕皮、在别处重新聚合，形成维度裂隙般的结构突变。鼓机编程展现出令人羡慕的控制力，breakbeat在折叠自身节奏后成为全新的东西。合成器层次复杂且持续处于即将成为别物的状态，lo-fi质感与高清清晰度并存。tribal鼓、circus bells、proto-brass等异质元素被引入，在不稳定中达成出人意料的平衡。整体制作呈现出高度信息密度的声音偏差，拒绝固守单一语法，将类型视为原材料而非目的地，是一张面向未来的电子音乐原型。

items.body: Magic Hour is both accessible and deeply experimental with its mutant ambient approach. The sonic palette employs clicks and clacks, echoes, mechanical whirs, lost terrestrial train whistles, melodic forms, shattering forms, and human murmurs, sometimes slowing or speeding up local fields to gain an emotional edge. Continuous processes of deconstruction and reconstruction Magic Hour by FeLid   Time is not a reliable empirical concept, Magic Hour combines improvisational and accidental guitar sounds, lyrical ambient drones, and high-definition sound editing. Magic Hour is both accessible and deeply experimental with its mutant ambient approach. The sonic palette employs clicks and clacks, echoes, mechanical whirs, lost terrestrial train whistles, melodic forms, shattering forms, and human murmurs, sometimes slowing or speeding up local fields to gain an emotional edge. Sharp, jarring cuts where one familiar sound instantly morphs into a new field. Drawing on all available sonic materials—including instrumental sounds, electronics, fragments of recorded audio, and environmental sounds—FeLid creates tracks and improvisational live performances through continuous processes of deconstruction and reconstruction. So many examples. Sounds with backwards envelopes, where the natural decay of a noise happens before its sharp impact. Freezing a specific moment or target in complete temporal suspension. Magic Hour is the second album by Tokyo-based artist FeLid, who combines improvisational and accidental guitar sounds, lyrical ambient drones, and high-definition sound editing. His practice is designed as a shared exploration of the relationship between sound and space, inviting audiences to experience and discover these connections together in real time. FeLid is the solo project of Kazutoshi Eguchi. He is known as a member of the post-hardcore band the north end and as a co-organizer of the festival platform MIMINOIMI. A collage of percussion instruments :: I am imagining dry mountain water, such as found in a Japanese rock garden. “Karesansui in the air #2” (5:14) opens into a collage of percussion instruments, wooden objects being tapped or struck, a curiously nourishing soup of casual fast easy flowing sounds. Here the passage of time is an objective measure. “Hello, World” (3:37) might be a welcome transparent soup of small items. Behind everything there is steamy condensation dripping and falling into a puddle on the ground, forming clusters with little gaps. Next the beat is bubbling and walking by itself, the feeling brings little scenes that open and close, and return, “Magic hour (disco)” (4:37). The ticking of the clock machinery is dark and hidden things are happening all around. The next thing I remember, I awakened in an “Environmental Mood” (3:13). We are washing stuff in the cave, bumping and scrubbing, spilling water and tossing things around, the scrubbing is the beat. Time to go to work. “Rotate Dub” (3:30) has musical lathes, a running motor sound of some kind, chattering and rattles, perhaps close views of many different motors not all at once, the power tools sing and purr. Do you feel like an afternoon rain shower? “Yuudachi Dub #2” (2:44) brings a different lathe creature here, chattering away faster, sometimes speeding like a demon, with a jittery beat, moving really quickly along, faces appear flattened in the direction they are traveling, the clock on board stretches. Our spaceship appears to move very slowly. Hold on, this next track is less than a minute in duration, “Akirame Mo Kanzin” (0:58). Metal stuff and small percussion instruments are being tapped, played backwards and forwards, very busy until the end, that occurs in an apparently irreversible succession from the past, through the present, and into the future. Now I am floating in the dark waters, “Harmonics Dub” (1:51), barely bobbing on the surface. I love the sound of guitar harmonics, textures made by energizing the strings, a mandolin being dusted off, searching for something. This turns out to lead into a haunted house, where we can play ping pong, “Sense of Gradation” (5:56) blends drone like textures with the steady ping pong tok tok tok sounds, a sound collage of real-world noises that have been warped, looped, and recontextualized into an abstract sonic experience, never busy, accenting the constant drone​ of imaginary wire strings being provoked, while the ping pong activities continue, proving the ability to use magic related to time. FeLid is also a member of MIMINOIMI, an organizing collective dedicated to exploring ambient and experimental music from multiple perspectives, and is involved in the planning and production of the urban festival Ambient / Week. Magic Hour is available on ato.archives. [Bandcamp] Magic Hour by FeLidThe post FeLid :: Magic Hour (ato.archives) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.

items._cn_summary: 这是东京艺术家FeLid（江口一利）的第二张专辑，以突变环境音乐为核心展开探索。作品将即兴与偶然产生的吉他声响、抒情氛围长音、高精度声音编辑融为一体，构成持续解构与重建的创作过程。声响素材涵盖打击乐器拼贴、木质物体敲击、回声、机械嗡鸣、火车汽笛、人声呢喃等，并通过场录材料的变速处理获取情感张力。专辑擅长制造逆向包络的声音——自然衰减先于尖锐冲击出现，或将某一瞬间冻结于时间的完全静止中。乐评特别提到《Karesansui in the air #2》以打击乐器开场，构建出枯山水庭院般的干燥质感；《Hello, World》呈现透明小品的蒸汽凝露意象；《Magic hour (disco)》则暗藏时钟机械的滴答节奏。整体体现艺术家对声音与空间关系的现场探索，适合关注实验声响设计、氛围音乐与田野录音融合的听众。

items.body: Review by Chaoticreason — 4 .5 stars.It is difficult to add any more eloquent words than Fernando has already said. It took me more than a few plays to grasp this work. That is a good thing, all too often find something immediately likeable, then wonder why I liked it a week later I hate it. However, this album has longevity, as I also believe the band has.This is a band that will stay the course, with the brilliant, and classically trained Nat Bergrin at the helm, this music is a true delight for all fans of the more progressive/experimental side of rock.Whilst I think it's fair to say that most of us love retro-sounding bands, you will only get glimpses of that from this most excellent and progressive of albums.When I first played disc, I thought "Oh wow!" a garage rock band playing very complex prog rock, which I do still stand by in some ways. But the technicality of all the players involved pushes it well beyond a garage rock band in any conventional sense. I love that they are a not a paint by numbers neo rock band. This is a band pushing musical boundaries, and I love the direction that they are taking. I love their earlier album 'Heart of a Cherry Pit Sun', but this album enters a whole new realm. This is an album well worth checking out, if your penchant is for progressive Jazz, Classical, black metal... etc. etc....In fact, if you really love the progression of progressive rock music, then this is not a band to be missed.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由受过古典训练的Nat Bergrin领衔，融合前卫摇滚、爵士与古典音乐的多重元素。评论者最初将其误认为车库摇滚乐队演奏复杂前卫摇滚，但乐手们的高超技术性迅速超越了任何传统车库摇滚的框架。专辑并非按部就班的复古致敬，而是积极拓展音乐边界，涉及前卫爵士、古典乃至黑金属等多种风格的交叉渗透。与乐队前作《Heart of a Cherry Pit Sun》相比，本作进入了一个全新的领域，展现出持久耐听的可重访价值。这是一支拒绝成为数字拼贴式新派摇滚乐队的团体，持续在实验性与结构感之间寻找平衡点。

items.body: Band: Kraanerg | Album: Aria for Labellum Tongues | Genre: Avant-prog | Year: 2026 From: Minneapolis, USA | Label: Independent For fans of: Frank Zappa, Papangu, Sigh, Cardiacs Bandcamp Kraanerg is the brainchild of composer and multi-instrumentalist Nat Bergrin, and Aria for Labellum Tongues is their third full-length release (and their second as a full band). This was my first exposure to Kraanerg, and I was very impressed by what I encountered. Western classical music plays a massive role on this record, both in terms of instrumentation and structure. Plenty of bands will shoehorn in some violin, but not many display the ability to integrate classical influences quite like this band does. “Amargosa Raga” kicks the album off with strange, discordant guitar lines. The vocal line is surprisingly melodic for the harsh, microtonal backing, and there’s some great supporting saxophone. Classical elements play a significant role here as well, with violin and piano taking the lead on various passages. What began as a fairly harsh piece gradually evolves into a lush composition, evoking many of the Mellotron-heavy greats of the classic prog era, but run through a more modern and uncompromisingly weird lens. The title track comes next, with an onslaught of buzzy guitars, swooping strings, and tinkling vibraphone. The classical influences on this track tread a fine line between sweet and creepy, with the violin frequently adding a remorseful edge.  “Blessings in Silk, Saffron, and Naran-Ji” nearly feels like a new wave song in its opening moments. There’s a bright hopefulness, but that soon gives way to a stripped-back classical passage. Piano, violin, and scratchy clean guitar float about. The intensity of the song gradually swells with the addition of drums and wordless vocals, lifting everything upward, but with an underlying sense of tension. When rock elements eventually take the lead again, violin remains the most prominent instrument. There’s an irrepressible sense of drama, and the somewhat rough vocals feel genuinely emotional. This piece is followed by the only song under four minutes on the album, “Anguloa Virginalis (Um Rosto de Mulher)”. It’s a light and airy breather following the intensity of the previous song. Piano, vibraphone, and delicate percussion evoke loungey jazz. Gothic organ and distorted guitar kicks off “Iron Sign of the Masdevallia”. Syncopated drums and piano give this track a disorienting feel, and the dense arrangement is smothering. As the song enters an instrumental section, sax and piano both get ample time in the spotlight, each one painting a dramatic picture. Next, the song takes a surprisingly sunny turn, with piano plinking out over a (mostly) major-key backing. The guitars borrow a lot from punk, but just about everything else is more clearly indebted to classical music, which makes for an interesting contrast. This artsy punk-fusion continues as this epic enters its final few minutes. The chords become more chaotic and irregular, and the vocals become more unhinged. The music is intense, yet oddly joyous, like Cardiacs’ best work. The opening gothic passage comes back for a closing reprise, which ties things up beautifully. The album ends on its longest song, the 20-minute “Visible to the Wrong Faces”. In comparison to the storming tempo of the previous song, this one is quite restrained in its opening. Classical music predominates for the first few minutes, led by piano and saxophone. It isn’t until about four minutes in that any rock elements enter, when buzzing guitars and stomping drums begin to play supporting roles. When vocals finally enter, the music is noisy with a sense of carefully-crafted chaos. Vibraphone and violin support jangly, post-punk guitars, and the vocal melody draws from avant-garde music. Throughout this whole album, the band has shown that they are masters of textural variation and contrast, and the second half of this song is a prime example. Post-metal, classical music, and classic prog influences are all evident, and everything gels into a satisfying conclusion. Aria for Labellum Tongues is a highly ambitious and very successful musical statement. The blending of rock and classical structures is pulled off wonderfully, and each of the songs on this album feels thoughtfully put-together. It’s a long and challenging record, but it’s well worth your time. Score: 95/100
items._cn_summary: Kraanerg由作曲家兼多乐器演奏者Nat Bergrin主导，这是其第三张全长专辑，也是作为完整乐队录制的第二张作品。整张专辑以西方古典音乐为核心结构框架，将小提琴、钢琴、颤音琴等古典乐器与失真吉他、萨克斯管、微调音和声乐编织在一起。开场曲从刺耳的不和谐吉他线条出发，逐渐演化为层次丰富的复调织体，在粗粝与抒情之间反复切换。标题曲以嗡嗡作响的吉他、滑奏的弦乐和阴郁的小提琴制造紧张感。多首作品在古典、朋克、新浪潮、爵士等风格之间自由穿梭，如钢琴与单簧管在偏主流调性中突然插入不对称节拍，形成戏剧性的反差。独立厂牌发行，明尼阿波利斯地下场景出身，是一张融合学院派作曲技法与前卫摇滚能量的实验性作品。

items.body:
After decades contributing to records where a single riff could transform a dancefloor, Charlie May turns that instinct inward on Trusted Farms. 

 For over thirty years, Charlie has occupied a position that seems increasingly rare in electronic music: the musician’s musician, the person behind the machines, the extra pair of hands in the studio, and quite often, the person responsible for the melody you end up carrying around in your head for weeks on end. 

 Alongside Duncan Forbes as Spooky, Charlie helped shape some of the most important electronic music to emerge from the UK in the early ’90s. That partnership would also sow the seeds for one of Sasha’s defining records: the central riff behind Xpander began life in Spooky’s live material, before Charlie brought the idea into the studio with Sasha and helped transform it into one of electronic music’s most enduring anthems.

 astrangelyisolatedplace · ASIPV058 Charlie May / Trusted Farms [PREVIEWS] 

 Listen closely to Charlie’s work and there’s a particular instinct that keeps returning: knowing when a simple synth line is enough. Knowing which note needs to change. Knowing when repetition stops being repetition and starts becoming the entire reason a track works. More recently, as one-third of Quiet Places on ASIP, he’s taken those same instincts somewhere looser — beatless, gridless and led by improvisation.

 Trusted Farms puts those instincts front and centre.

 Tiny melodic phrases appear and refuse to leave. Synth lines repeat just long enough to become lodged in your head. Parts rub against each other without being tidied into submission. There’s a sharpness and directness to it all amongst the purposeful analogue warmth.

 Some of these tracks feel almost ridiculously simple at first. But simplicity is difficult when you’ve spent decades learning every possible way to complicate something. Many of the parts on Trusted Farms were performed live with minimal editing. A synth line might be doubled, distorted, re-recorded and pushed back through another piece of equipment, but it remains the same idea. Instead of filling the gaps, Charlie works on the weight and character of what is already there. The melodies become physical; slightly worn around the edges.

 For someone whose fingerprints can be found across some genuinely monumental moments in electronic music, Charlie has spent decades knowing what to add. Trusted Farms is about knowing exactly what to leave alone.

 Available on black 12” and digital, mastered by Andreas Lupo LOOP-O Lubich and featuring artwork by Peter Skwiot Smith, Trusted Farms will be available on October 16th 2026.

items._cn_summary: Charlie May 三十余年来以幕后音乐人身份参与塑造了英国电子音乐的关键时刻，其中最广为人知的是与 Sasha 合作《Xpander》核心旋律的构思。专辑《Trusted Farms》将这种旋律直觉内化为独立作品的核心语言：简短的合成器乐句反复出现并驻留脑中，未经剪辑的现场演奏配合模拟设备的再处理，使每条旋律在保留原始意图的同时获得磨损般的物理质感。整体制作克制而精确，大量减法式的编排取代了堆叠与填满，重复在临界点上转化为结构本身。作为 A Strangely Isolated Place 厂牌发行的延续性作品，此专辑与他参与的三人组合 Quiet Places 一脉相承，在节拍与自由即兴之间寻找平衡点。

items.body: Rather than treating glitch as surface decoration, Signal_Black builds an entire skeletal language around it. What emerges is a unified, tightly constructed collection of focused (yet splintered) electronics—one that pushes exploratory sound forward through distortion, fragmentation, and a distinctly futuristic sense of movement. A distinctly futuristic sense of movement Revealed several months ago in April 2026, this sleek eight-piece suite (titled Disruptive Event) still carries a sense of propulsion and precise direction. From its opening moments, Signal_Black (aka Marcin) establishes a dense exchange between analog glitch and Autechre-influenced sound-design, immediately evident on “Higher Ground.” From there, the project descends deep below terra firma, evolving through scraped emotive melodic fragments and moving further into ambient-industrial IDM abstraction. A fixation on roughened rhythms and microscopic melodic fibers gives “Internal Merge” its distinctive tension, folding broken structures into looping forms that gradually become cohesive without losing their instability. “Long Now” shifts toward wobbling bass pressure, while “TON” sinks into darker ambient territory, and what becomes more evident is that each track extends the artist’s interest in malfunction, texture, and controlled disorientation. As the final pieces move through old-school Arovane-like finesse, especially on “Text of The Present,” “Chronic” delivers a more microscopic form of sonic deformation. Its fractured detail reflects the album’s central idea: a disruptive event capable of interrupting established operations, routines, or systems. Rather than treating glitch as surface decoration, Signal_Black builds an entire skeletal language around it. What emerges is a unified, tightly constructed collection of focused (yet splintered) electronics—one that pushes exploratory sound forward through distortion, fragmentation, and a distinctly futuristic sense of movement. While Disruptive Event channels our favored old-school IDM mechanics associated with Richard Devine, Gescom, Funckarma, Alva Noto, SND, and Funkstörung, Signal_Black takes that lineage somewhere altogether stranger—refining tone, deepening texture, and redirecting momentum into a galaxy of its own. Disruptive Event is available on Evel. [Bandcamp] Disruptive Event by Signal_BlackThe post Signal_Black :: Disruptive Event (Evel) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: Signal_Black的《Disruptive Event》围绕glitch构建了一套完整的骨架式语言体系，而非将其仅作表面装饰。专辑共八首作品，以模拟故障与Autechre式声音设计为核心，从开篇便确立了密集的电子对话，随后逐步沉入地表之下，经历刮擦式情感旋律碎片，最终进入环境工业与IDM抽象地带。破碎结构被折叠成循环形态，在不稳定中逐渐凝聚张力。专辑后半段在Arovane式精致与微观声学变形之间切换，每首曲目都在延续对故障、质感与受控迷失的探索。评论将其置于Richard Devine、Gescom、Funckarma等经典IDM谱系中，但指出Signal_Black将这条线索引向了更为陌生的方向——精炼音色、深化纹理、重新导向运动感，形成独属于创作者自身的星系。整体而言，这是一张统一而紧凑的电子专辑，兼具推进力与精确方向感。

items.body: That exchange between past and present is central to Axial Opposition. Classic Multiplex structures remain recognizable, yet the melodic synthesis gives them renewed dimension, allowing vintage electronic language to exist alongside contemporary detail. A duo creating electronics with melody as its backbone [PCLLP 037] Axial Opposition by Multiplex   Multiplex are brothers Christian and Roland Dormon, their focused frenzy of pulsating electronics sees no barriers, but always anchored by a deep melodic instinct. Emerging from IDM’s early days more than two decades ago—recall their releases with Toytronic, Senton, Piehead, and U-Cover)— they now find a home with Belarus-based People Can Listen following recent releases Colour Kinetica (Bricolage) and Human, I Love You (w/ Remixes) (Clean Error). Their historical relevance remains an important factoid for anyone new to sandblasted, ever-veering strains of broken beats, IDM, and melodic electro, yet beneath those fractured forms is where Multiplex have always been most distinctive: tuneful synthesis, layered with ambient propulsion and shaped into electronic structures that feel both precise and uniquely alive. Axial Opposition opens with punishing electro, eerily transcendental in its summation of the 42-second opener “Reality (Interlude),” before settling into their bread-and-butter language of pristine melodies, glowing synth lines, and carefully interlocked sound design textures. Synthesizers are not simply used as rhythmic machinery here; they carry the emotional weight, allowing melodies to drift, repeat, fracture, and return with a nostalgic clarity. That sensibility comes to life across favorites such as “In Your Dreams,” “Pulsar Energy,” “Verhn,” “Aditya,” and “Neeta_x,” before dissolving into the closing atmospheric layers of “Implode (outro).” “What makes the collection compelling is how naturally those eras communicate: older synth ideas are not merely revived, but repolished, expanded, and brought into the present without losing their original character.” ~Pietro Da Sacco With 24 years now behind Pinghaus Frequencies (Toytronic), alongside earlier productions dating to 1999, Multiplex have long signalled a duo creating electronics with melody as its backbone. Axial Opposition gathers new and vintage material after more than 15 years of silence, sending music back and forth between studios, adding elements along the way and shaping everything into a final mix. What makes the collection compelling is how naturally those eras communicate: older synth ideas are not merely revived, but repolished, expanded, and brought into the present without losing their original character. That exchange between past and present is central to Axial Opposition. Classic Multiplex structures remain recognizable, yet the melodic synthesis gives them renewed dimension, allowing vintage electronic language to exist alongside contemporary detail. There is nostalgia here, but it never feels archival; sounds that might have belonged to another era are given fresh circuitry, fresh atmosphere, and a new context. After such a long silence, Multiplex return not by abandoning what made their sound distinctive, but by reconnecting with it and pushing it forward. A multiverse of melodic electronics, where old synthesis is made new again, and one that only Multiplex can navigate so well. Axial Opposition is available on People Can Listen. items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Frank Zappa's "pastiche" technique had taken on a new immediacy and a breakneck pace starting with Over-Nite Sensation, when Ian Underwood (saxophones and flute) joined Sal Marquez (trumpet) and George Duke (keyboards) and, notably, this marked the first time Jean-Luc Ponty was a member of his regular band (which included musicians from the Mothers of Invention alongside the Big-Band lineup that began with Waka/Jawaka). With the follow-up album, Apostrophe ('), the music went a step further compositionally, reformulating genres through Zappa's unique stamp combined with the contributions of the virtuoso group he had surrounded himself with.In "Don't Eat the Yellow Snow," he sang rapidly and the band played at a fast pace, except when they shifted the rhythm for comedic effect. This embodied the Dadaist approach that defined his music and his deconstruction of familiar forms, an approach that could lead to paradoxes, such as in "Nanook Rubs It," where he tackled jazz by singing in the style of Tom Waits's spoken-word delivery, ironically, after Waits himself had served as his opening act in the early 70s and struggled to win over the audience. There was psychedelia interwoven with soul, yet nothing quite like what we knew; the backing vocals contributed significantly to the band's sound, a sound truly unfathomable within the Zappa universe.Atonal music, specifically the contemporary classical style of Schoenberg and Var�se (the very same artist to whom Chicago dedicated their track "A Hit by Var�se") could be seen distilled within "St. Alfonzo's Pancake Breakfast." This represented a challenging exercise in synthesizing that entire musical world, an approach he would explore in greater depth years later on one of his masterpieces, One Size Fits All."Father O'Blivion" is a jazz-rock track that shifts into cosmic and progressive territory with effortless ease, a mere turn of a few notes, always possessing that knack for making highly complex music sound deceptively simple. "Cosmik Debris" was a blend of blues and soul, punctuated and interwoven by the invisible, precise stitches of Ruth Underwood's percussion. Zappa adopted a highly suggestive Barry White-esque persona, yet his guitar playing was raw, wild, and distorted; one could never predict where a solo or a riff might lead. He was truly many figures rolled into one: singer, guitarist, composer, and, of course, orchestra conductor."Excentrifugal Forz" speaks for itself right from the title, highlighting the force that emanated from his music during that era, a time when even rock was an indivisible whole. The same can be said for the track "Apostrophe", featuring Jack Bruce on bass, which sounds dense, powerful, and heavy; it emerged from an unexpected jam session and was captured that way forever. The bass and guitar tones of Zappa and Bruce meshed perfectly, creating a contrast that thrived within the stereo mix. It is a tour-de-force, especially considering how the wild playing styles of McLaughlin and Zappa represent such vastly different extremes."Uncle Remus" provided a fantastic counterpoint at this stage of the �lbum, a sort of veiled tribute to Dr. John, featuring New Orleans-style gospel and rhythm & blues courtesy of George Duke. Stink-Foot had a distinctive way of recording the instruments, incorporating echoes, shifts in mood and atmosphere, and killer guitar solos that, much like the electric keyboard, would break into that jazzy-blues vibe.Apostrophe (') is the crucial link that, following Over-Nite Sensation, would give rise to One Size Fits All; it stands out by showcasing Zappa's signature style, transforming what was essentially a deconstructed transitional period into a distinct era in its own right.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续并发展了作者独特的拼贴技法，编曲上以高密度、多元融合为核心路径。乐队编制横跨爵士管乐、键盘、打击乐与电声乐器，将无调性序列音乐、迷幻、灵魂乐与爵士摇滚熔于一炉，呈现出荒诞又精密的复合质感。多首曲目中，快速念白与节奏骤变交替，制造出解构体裁的喜剧张力；与Jack Bruce合作的同名曲则从即兴jam中捕捉到厚重的贝斯与吉他互动。整体上，专辑在类型边界上高度模糊，既有无调性古典的凝练，也有放克律动的松散，展现出作者将复杂构思伪装为直觉音乐的能力。

items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items.body: Valencia label Industrial Complexx reissues the various-artists compilation “SUICIDE Tribute To Iconic New York Legends” on double cassette and digital on October 15, 2026. The 18-track set, originally released by Unknown Pleasures Records in 2014, gathers international minimal synth, electro-punk and industrial acts covering the catalogue of Suicide’s Alan Vega and Martin Rev. SUICIDE Tribute To Iconic New York Legends by Various Artists The reissue accompanies the Spanish-language publication of “Suicide, delincuentes electrónicos,” an essay on the band by musician and writer Pedro Peñas y Robles, originally published in French and English in 2024 and now released in Spanish by Industrial Complexx. The book traces the duo’s genesis and the chaotic sessions behind their 1977 debut album, drawing on testimony from scene figures including Marc Hurtado of Étant Donnés. ‘SUICIDE Tribute To Iconic New York Legends’ contributors The tribute pairs Vega and Rev’s original catalogue with reinterpretations from Distel, Radical G, The Horrorist, David Carretta and Jürgen Engler of Die Krupps, Növö, Adan+Ilse featuring Gabi Delgado of D.A.F., Marc Hurtado performing with Alan Vega himself, Liebknecht featuring Kristoffer Grip of Agent Side Grinder, Unknown Celebrities, Laag, Position Parallele, Cruise [ctrl] featuring Richard 23 and Patrick Codenys of Front 242, The Present Moment, Absolute Body Control, Millimetric featuring Dirk Da Davo of The Neon Judgement, Black Egg featuring hausfrau, Simi Nah featuring KGB, and In Death It Ends featuring Usher of Norma Loy. Covered songs include “Che,” “Ghost Rider,” “Cheree,” “Frankie Teardrop,” “Dream Baby Dream” and “Diamonds, Fur Coat, Champagne.” Industrial Complexx describes the collection as channeling “the same abrasive, alienating and futuristic energy” that shaped Suicide’s catalogue. About Suicide Suicide was an American duo formed in New York City in 1970 by vocalist Alan Vega and instrumentalist Martin Rev, initially a trio with guitarist Paul Liebgott before continuing as a two-piece. The group paired Vega’s stream-of-conscious, rockabilly-inflected vocals with Rev’s minimal synthesizer and drum-machine backing, and was among the first acts to use the term “punk music” to describe itself, in 1970. Suicide independently released its debut album, “Suicide,” in 1977 on Red Star Records, featuring “Ghost Rider,” “Frankie Teardrop” and “Cheree.” A second album, “Suicide: Alan Vega and Martin Rev,” followed in 1980 on Ze Records, then “A Way of Life” in 1988, “Why Be Blue” in 1992 and the final studio album, “American Supreme,” in 2002. Vega and Rev also worked separately: Vega collaborated with Andrew Eldritch of The Sisters of Mercy as The Sisterhood in 1986, and with Alex Chilton and Ben Vaughn on “Cubist Blues” in 1996, while both released solo albums throughout their careers. Suicide played its final concert at London’s Barbican Centre on July 9, 2015, before Alan Vega died on July 16, 2016, at age 78. “SUICIDE Tribute To Iconic New York Legends,” first released via Unknown Pleasures Records in 2014, returns via Industrial Complexx on October 15, 2026, alongside the Spanish edition of Pedro Peñas y Robles’s book on the band.
items._cn_summary: 西班牙厂牌 Industrial Complexx 重新发行了这张向纽约传奇二人组 Suicide 致敬的合辑，收录 18 首翻唱作品，涵盖多位欧洲暗潮与工业领域的重要艺术家，包括 Die Krupps、D.A.F.、Front 242、Absolute Body Control、The Neon Judgement 等乐队的成员参与。重新发行以双卡带和数字形式呈现，同时伴随西班牙语版 Suicide 传记随附出版。选曲覆盖 Suicide 经典曲目如《Ghost Rider》《Frankie Teardrop》《Cheree》《Dream Baby Dream》等，原作以极简合成器、机械鼓机与神经质的演唱为标志，被该合辑诠释为保留了粗糙、疏离与未来感的核心气质。整张合辑既是经典后朋克/工业先驱的回顾，也是当下欧洲地下电子场景对其遗产的集体回应。

items.body: One half of the Senior Staff was able to get out to a wholly non-ID:UD related gig over the weekend and catch Calgary’s Mares Of Thrace play a very rhythmically tight and cathartic set of doom metal. As we’ve briefly discussed here and there we’re both fans of a decent amount of metal covering a number of sub-genres, but neither of us are experts. Frankly, sometimes its nice to switch off the part of your brain that needs to be developing informed opinions and producing thoughtful analysis at all times and just enjoy some music simply because you dig it. But speaking of thoughtful analysis (?), let’s get you back to the home front with this week’s tracks. Dismantled Godflesh, “Master And Slave” Justin Broadrick announced earlier this year that he’d be winding Godflesh down for a second time some fifteen-odd years after its reactivation, but was planning two full LPs of new material before that time comes. The first such record sees release on Friday, and while the ratio of dub, electronic, and breaks elements which have always flitted about Godflesh releases had perhaps increased over the last few post-reunion albums, it’s hard not to think that Decay will be going right for the jugular Streetcleaner style based on its opening track. Turn it up and revel in the soothing annihilation of that bass tone. Decay by GODFLESH Grendel, “Dominion” It’s somehow been 7 years since the release of Grendel’s last LP Ascending the Abyss. It’s been a tangible absence in Our offices; JD Tucker has spent the last decade and a half redefining his legacy as an electro-industrial stylist and producer, starting with 2012’s genre-defying Timewave: Zero and the superlative Age of the Disposable Body, the latter being legitimately one of the most important political albums of the 2010s in Our Thing. “Dominion” speaks to the band we’ve come to know Grendel to be while showing some intriguing developments, such as JD’s now accomplished melodic vocal style, some very smooth string programming and sleek modern sound design applied to a classic EBM gallop. All that and lyrics that don’t just decry the social media era but examine the panopticon of control they emerge from? Welcome back Grendel, we missed you. Dominion by Grendel Dismantled, “Zero” Speaking of long-awaited returns, holy shit, there’s new Dismantled. Gary Zon’s long-running project has always been a standard bearer for a version of hard and harsh electro-industrial that maintains the genre’s atmospheric and emotional core. The first track from the forthcoming Endless is “Zero”, a cut that features Zon’s distinctive processed and multi-layered vocals, samples, and some fine string programming for good measure. It’s melancholic, but after a more than half a decade wait (the album was originally teased all the way back in 2021), it’s a sound that feels right. Endless by Dismantled Rosetta Stone, “Shadowban” Porl King’s moved Rosetta Stone through a number of preceding modes since reactivating the legendary second wave of goth rock project as a solo joint seven years back. A forthcoming release looks to keep that trend going (the Executing Nostalgia title feels rather on the nose in that regard) – one half of it will be made up of classic goth covers, continuing in the tradition of Unerotica and last year’s Nothing Is Sacred, while the other half is originals. This first taste of the latter feels like a callback to a very different moment in King’s history, though: the claustrophobic and hazy bass fog of this cut’s a dead ringer for the post witch house loops and grooves which made up the bulk of the voluminous In Death It Ends catalog in the 2010s. Shadowban by Rosetta Stone Control Fields, “Black Anomaly” Some solidly chewy bass sits at the centre of the B-side of the debut single from Tbilisi producer Control Fields, but that’s not the only thing which has us flashing back to 90s EBM and dark electro. The combo of icy programming and classic “hacking the Gibson” style sampling on this goes down as smooth as a Jolt cola being slammed during an all night Quake LAN party. Friction Code by Control Fields Emmon, “Relics (Kris Baha remix)” Kris Baha is one of the most reliable producers that emerged from the techno-body moment, with his canny grasp of gnarly sound design and how to assemble peak time bangers making him a go-to remixer for many artists. For evidece of why and the results why not check out Baha’s mix for Emmon’s “Relics”, taking the pensive and punchy original and giving it a slick peak-time makeover that references breakbeat driven 90’s techno, some psytrance, and some seriously warped synthwork. This’ll singe your nosehairs if you aren’t careful, play loud with caution. The post Tracks: September 21st, 2026 appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 本期乐评聚焦多支乐队新作：Godflesh 宣布即将再次解散，但在此之前先带来新专辑《Decay》，首支单曲回归早期《Streetcleaner》式的工业金属压迫感，贝斯音色极具重量。Grendel 时隔七年回归，新单曲展现成熟的旋律人声与现代电子音效设计，在传统 EBM 节拍骨架上融入弦乐编程与社交媒体控制论主题。Gary Zon 领军的 Dismantled 终于释出苦等五年的专辑《Endless》首曲，多层处理人声与采样编织出阴郁而情绪饱满的电子工业质感。此外乐评人还现场聆听了加拿大卡尔加里 Mares Of Thrace 的末日金属演出，盛赞其节奏紧凑且具有宣泄力。整体来看，本期推荐曲目在工业与电子工业领域均呈现扎实的声音设计与题材深度。

items.body: 「世界3大ジャズ・フェス」に数えられるスイスのモントルー・ジャズ・フェスティバル（Montreux Jazz Festival）。これまで幅広いジャンルのミュージシャンが熱演を繰り広げてきたこのフェスの特徴は、50年を超える歴史を通じてライブ音源と映像が豊富にストックされている点にある。その中からCD、DVD、デジタル音源などでリリースされている「名盤」を紹介していく。 アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム、あるいはダラー・ブランド。アパルトヘイト下の南アフリカでジャズの演奏を始め、その後国外に逃れて音楽活動を続けた名ピアニストが91年の長い人生を終えたのは、今年(2026年)の6月だった。ソロ、デュオ、トリオ、コンボ、オーケストラと、あらゆるフォーマットで作品を残した彼の音楽のエッセンスに触れられるのが、1980年のモントルー・ジャズ・フェスティバルの記録『アット・モントルー』である。そのアルバムを紹介しながら、彼のキャリアを偲ぶ。 『アフリカン・ピアノ』の衝撃 ダラー・ブランドがイスラム教に改宗し、名をアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムとしたのは1968年である。彼の代表作として知られる『アフリカン・ピアノ』が、デンマークの首都コペンハーゲンでライブ録音されたのは69年だから、その時点で彼はすでにアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムになっていたことになる。しかし彼は、ダラー・ブランドとしてその後しばらく活動を続けた。 『アフリカン・ピアノ』の名義は、現行盤ではアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムとなっているが、長らくダラー・ブランド名義で流通してきた。ダラー・ブランドという名の方が現在でも通りがいいのは、ひとえに『アフリカン・ピアノ』の圧倒的な知名度による。 もっとも、ダラー・ブランドという名も実は本名ではなく、出生名をアドルフ・ヨハネス・ブランドといった。ダラーとは「ドル」のことで、南アフリカの故郷ケープタウンの港に寄港した水兵にドル札を渡してジャズのSP盤を熱心に収集していたことで、ダラーが彼のニックネームとなったのだった。 名作『アフリカン・ピアノ』の原盤権を当初持っていたのは、デンマークで1969年から72年までの短い期間活動したスペクテイター・レコードだった。73年になってECMのサブ・レーベルであるJAPOからリリースされたことで、このアルバムは広く世界に知られることになった。現在では、この作品はECMを代表するピアノ・ソロ作としての地位を不動のものにしている。アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムのほかのアルバムは聴いたことがなくても、『アフリカン・ピアノ』は何度も聴いたというジャズ・ファンはわが国でも少なくないと思う。 70年代初頭と言えば、モダン・ジャズが雑多な要素を吸収して鵺（ぬえ）のような音楽に変貌しつつあった頃だが、その時代でも『アフリカン・ピアノ』は奇異な作品であったと思う。延々と繰り返される反復フレーズ。スコールのように畳みかける旋律。隙間なく連続し、どこが始まりでどこが終わりか判然としない楽曲──。それは、アメリカのジャズ、あるいはアメリカの黒人音楽とは明らかに異質な音楽だった。 南アが生んだ3人の世界的ミュージシャン 現在聴くことができるアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムの最も古い録音は、ジャズ・エピッスルズというセクステットによるもので、レコーディングは1959年であった。このバンドには、やはりのちに世界的なミュージシャンとなるトランペッターのヒュー・マセケラも在籍していた。マセケラが「グレイジング・イン・ザ・グラス」で全米1位を獲得するのは68年のことである。 ジャズ・エピッスルズのメンバーのうち3人は、南ア初の黒人ミュージカル『キング・コング』に参加していて、マセケラもそのひとりだった。『キング・コング』のヒロインとして舞台に立ったのがミリアム・マケバで、彼女もまたのちに世界的シンガーとなる。マセケラとマケバは、わずか2年だが結婚していたこともあった。アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム、ヒュー・マセケラ、ミリアム・マケバ。南アが生んだこの3人のスターが同じコミュニティから出発したのは、南アのジャズ・シーンそのものが小さなコミュニティだったからである。 ジャズ・エピッスルズは、南アで公式に発売された初めての黒人ジャズ・バンドのレコードだった。『ヴァース1』がそのタイトルだったが、『ヴァース2』が録音されることはついになかった。アパルトヘイト下の南アにあって、黒人ならびにその音楽であるジャズに対する弾圧がほどなく激化したことがその理由である。 南ア独自のタウンシップ・ジャズ 1994年まで南アフリカの政権を握ったNP（国民党）が、悪名高い人種分離政策であるアパルトヘイトを掲げたのは1948年だった。南ア人は、「白人」「カラード」「インド人」「アフリカ人」の4つのカテゴリーに分けられ、結婚やセックスによる人種混淆を妨げる法律が整備されて、居住区の分割や都市における人種隔離が進められた。 人種の分類上、ヒュー・マセケラとミリアム・マケバは「アフリカ人」、アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムは白人と黒人の混血である「カラード」であった。3人はいずれも1960年代に母国をあとにしたが、その後マセケラとマケバが90年代まで一度も帰国が叶わなかったのに対し、イブラヒムは何度か国に帰ることを許されている。これは、「アフリカ人」と「カラード」の法的権利の違いによるものだったと思われる。 人種分離は、トイレ、レストラン、ホテル、劇場から、バス、学校、役場にまで及び、社会生活のあらゆる領域が「ヨーロッパ人」向けと「非ヨーロッパ人」向けに分けられた。「ヨーロッパ人」とは、南アへの初期入植者であるオランダ人と、その後入植してきたイギリス人を主に指す。 しかし、オランダ人とイギリス人の間にもまた格差はあって、南アの経済、政治、社会の上層を長らく支配してきたのはイギリス人だった。イギリス人支配に対するオランダ人のルサンチマンの結晶のような政党がNPで、その初期の構成員の多くは、戦時にあってナチス・ドイツを支持した者たちだった。政権を握った彼らが設計したアパルトヘイトの諸制度は、しばしばナチスのユダヤ人政策に比して語られる。 アパルトヘイトは、アメリカ南部で1860年代から100年間にわたって存続した人種差別法「ジム・クロウ法」にも似ていたが、それ以上に残酷であったのは、アメリカにはなかった黒人の強制移住があったことによる。 1923年に施行された原住民都市地域法という法律によって、黒人は「タウンシップ」と呼ばれた隔離居住区に住むことを強制された。最も古いタウンシップはイブラヒムの故郷であったケープタウンにあって、その後南ア全土にタウンシップが設けられた。ここで独自に発展したのが、タウンシップ・ジャズである。 アメリカのラグタイムやスウィングと南アの土着の音楽が混じり合って生まれたのがタウンシップ・ジャズで、そこにカリブ海の音楽の要素も感じられるのは、ニューオリンズを経由してもたらされた影響があったからかもしれない。また、南アはある時期までイギリスの旧植民地や入植地の共同体である英連邦の構成国であったから、同じく英連邦の国であったジャマイカやバルバドスから音楽が伝わるルートもおそらくあっただろう。 禁じられたジャズと音楽家たちの出国 1950年代になって、タウンシップ・ジャズと、その後に輸入されたアメリカのジャズをベースにしたジャズ・バンドがいくつか生まれた。ジャズ・エピッスルズがその代表格だったが、彼らが最初のアルバムをレコーディングしてほどなく、南ア史に残る事件が起きた。1960年3月21日の「シャープヴィル虐殺」である。 アパルトヘイト下の南アでは、黒人に身分証の常時携帯を義務づける「パス法」という法律があった。それに抗議するために南アの首都ヨハネスブルグ近郊シャープヴィルの警察署に集まった黒人群衆に警察が発砲した事件が「シャープヴィル虐殺」で、これによって69人が殺され、180人以上が負傷した。 反アパルトヘイト運動のリーダーであり、1962年に逮捕されて以後27年間を獄中で過ごしたのがネルソン・マンデラだった。アパルトヘイト撤廃後の新生南ア初の大統領に就任した彼の歩みを描いた映画『マンデラ 自由への長い道』に、シャープヴィル虐殺の場面が出てくる。犠牲者の多くは、警察の装甲車から逃げ惑う中、背後から無差別に撃たれたのだった。この事件は海外各国に衝撃を与え、国連は3月21日を国際人種差別撤廃デーと定めた。 この事件をきっかけに、南ア全土に抗議行動が広がり、それにともなって南ア政府の弾圧も激化した。ジャズの演奏やラジオでの放送も禁止され、ジャズ・エピッスルズは解散を余儀なくされた。その後、先の3人は故郷を後にすることになる。ヒュー・マセケラがロンドンに活動の場を移したのが1960年、アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムが欧州に移住したのが62年で、これはマンデラが逮捕されたのと同じ年であった。ミリアム・マケバは、反アパルトヘイト運動に関与した咎で、67年に国外追放されている。 サックス・プレーヤーとしてのイブラヒム 欧州に活動の場を求めたアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムの庇護者となったのが、デューク・エリントンだった。スイスにツアーで訪れていたエリントンにイブラヒムの演奏を聴くよう懇願したのは、彼の婚約者であったと伝わる。 イブラヒムのトリオの演奏を気に入ったエリントンは、この有望なピアニストのワールドワイドのデビュー作となる『デューク・エリントン・プレゼンツ・ザ・ダラー・ブランド・トリオ』のレコーディングを支援した。リリースされたのは、フランク・シナトラが1961年に設立したリプリーズ・レコードからだった。 その後イブラヒムは数々のアルバムをレコーディングすることになるが、最も多くのアルバムを残したのは、ドイツのレーベル、エンヤ（Enja）である。エンヤの設立は1971年で、これはECM設立の翌年に当たる。Enjaというレーベル名は「European New Jazz」の略で、この場合の「New」はアメリカのジャズに対して「新しい」のみならず、ECMよりもさらに「新しい」音楽を目指そうとする意気込みの表現でもあっただろう。 1980年、イブラヒムはモントルー・ジャズ・フェスティバルに出演して8曲を演奏した。うち6曲を収録したライブ盤がリリースされたのも、やはりエンヤからだった。 バンドは、アルト・サックス、トロンボーンをフロントに擁したクインテットだったが、冒頭の「ツァクヴェ」では明らかに3本の管の音が聞こえる。日本盤CDのライナーノーツには「3管を含むセクステットの一体感をアピールしている」という意味不明の記述があるが、3管に聞こえるのはイブラヒムもサックスを吹いているからである。 イブラヒムは、ピアノ以外にフルートやチェロなどを奏する多才な音楽家だった。モントルーではソプラノ・サックスを吹いていて、それがたんなる余技とは言えないのは、6曲中3曲でピアノを弾かずにソプラノを吹いているからだ。裏ジャケットのクレジットも「Soprano Saxophone, Piano」と、サックスが先になっている。 アルバムの最後の曲「イシュマエル」は、ベースの反復フレーズが延々と繰り返されるイブラヒムの代表曲のひとつだが、この曲で彼は堂々たるサックス・ソロを披露していて、吹き終えたのち、客席から大きな喝采を受けている。 イブラヒムの音楽の広大な世界 モントルーのライブ盤はわずか6曲だが、驚くほど多様であったイブラヒムの音楽がこの一枚に凝縮されていると感じる。タウンシップ・ジャズ、サンバ、アラビア音楽、デューク・エリントン、セロニアス・モンク──。これも彼の代表曲である「ザ・ウェディング」は、雑多な原料を混ぜ合わせ、それを蒸留したのちに残った原酒のように澄明で美しい。 アルト・サックスのほかにフルートも吹くカルロス・ワードはパナマ出身のプレーヤーで、ジョン・コルトレーン、ドン・チェリー、セシル・テイラーらとの共演で知られている。イブラヒムとは、ドン・チェリーとのトリオで録音した1972年のライブ盤『第三世界＝アンダーグラウンド／The Third World-Underground』からのつきあいであり、その後デュオ作も一緒にレコーディングしている。 『第三世界＝アンダーグラウンド』は何度も繰り返し聴きたくなる名作である。チェリーの個性が大いに発揮されているが、とくにアヴァンギャルドな作品ではない。このアルバムと、ソロ作の『アフリカン・ピアノ』、さらにオーケストラと共演した何枚かの作品のうちのひとつ、例えば『アフリカ組曲／African Suite』などをこのモントルーのライブ盤と合わせて聴けば、アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムの広大な世界の概要を知ることができると思う。エンヤにレコーディングされたアルバムから10曲をセレクトした『プレミアム・ベスト』というCDもまた、格好の手引きとなるだろう。 2011年のモアーズ・フェスティバルにて 独唱によって閉じられた長いキャリア 2024年、アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムはロンドンのバービカン・センターでコンサートを行い、その演奏をレコーディングした。フルート奏者と、ベース／チェロ奏者とのトリオによるライブで、そのアルバムに『3』というタイトルがつけられたのは、トリオ演奏であるからだけではなく、アルバムが3部構成になっているからである。 1部には、ライブ前の無観客のホールで、8トラックのアナログ・テープ・マシンで録音した6曲が収録されている。資料によれば、この機材はエルヴィス・プレスリーがデビュー曲「イッツ・オール・ライト」を録音した際に使ったものであり、メンフィスのサン・スタジオにあったその機材を現在所有しているのは、ブラーのデーモン・アルバーンだそうである。そのテープ・マシンを、デーモンのスタジオからバービカン・センターに運んで録音が行われたのだった。 2部、3部は客を入れたのちのライブ演奏で、2部ではイブラヒムのヒーローであったエリントンの「イン・ア・センチメンタル・ムード」と、ジョン・コルトレーンの「ジャイアント・ステップス」、3部ではセロニアス・モンクの「スキッピー」を演奏している。 2部と3部には「リプライズ」と題されたピアノ・ソロの演奏が収められているが、注意深く耳を傾ければ、その中にジャズ・エピッスルズの名曲「ブルース・フォー・ヒューイ」のメロディを聴くことができる。「ヒューイ」はヒュー・マセケラの愛称である。南アのジャズの歴史をともにつくった古い友に対する変わらぬ友情をイブラヒムは示そうとしたのかもしれない。マセケラの死去から6年が経っていた。 2回目のアンコールで、イブラヒムはアカペラで歌を歌っている。アフリカの民族語と英語をまじえて歌われるその歌には、「伝達──幾世紀の歴史をもつ海運貨物の音」というタイトルがつけられている。何世紀にもわたって海運で運ばれていった貨物。それが何を意味するか、言うまでもあるまい。 このアルバムが、結果的にアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムの遺作となった。アフリカの奴隷貿易の歴史を歌う独唱で、イブラヒムは長いキャリアを閉じた。彼の新作がもはや聴けなくなった今、残された膨大な作品の森にあらためて分け入りたく思う。 文／二階堂 尚 『At Montreux』 アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム／ダラー・ブランド ■1.Tsakve 2. Whoza Mtwana 3. The Homecoming Song 4. The Wedding 5. The Perfumed Forest Wet With Rain 6. Ismael ■アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム(ss,p)、カルロス・ワード(as,fl)、クレイグ・ハリス(tb)、アロンゾ・ガードナー(b)、アンドレ・ストロパート(ds) ■第14回モントルー・ジャズ・フェスティバル／1980年7月18日   投稿 【アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム】長い歩みを終えた南アフリカの名ピアニスト ─ライブ盤で聴くモントルー Vol.69 は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评纪念刚刚离世的南非钢琴家阿卜杜拉·伊布拉希姆，以1980年蒙特勒爵士音乐节的现场录音专辑《At Montreux》为线索，回溯其跨越数十年的音乐生涯。文章从1969年录制的代表作《African Piano》谈起，详述伊布拉希姆从美元·布兰德到皈依伊斯兰教改名的心路历程，以及ECM厂牌如何将这张钢琴独奏专辑推向世界。乐评穿插大量南非历史背景，包括种族隔离政策下黑人音乐人的遭遇、强制迁徙形成的隔离居住区，以及由此孕育出的独特爵士风格。文中还追溯了他与休·马塞克拉、米里亚姆·马凯巴等同乡音乐人的交集，以及南非爵士场景与加勒比音乐之间的渊源。整篇文章将音乐评介与历史文化叙事紧密结合，展现了一位非裔音乐人在压迫中坚守艺术创作的完整脉络。

items.body: Everybody Else’s Life, Too is the latest from Josh Berman, a stalwart of the Chicago scene still somewhat underappreciated outside of his hometown. He has played the gamut of Chicago improvisors (including Mars Williams’ A Very Ayler Xmas project, the all-too-short-lived Michael Zerrang and the Blue Lights, and Ken Vandermark’s Audio One), sneaked across the Atlantic to record with Paul Lytton, Edward Perraud, and Jon Rune Strøm, and led several of his own bands. On this one, he is joined by bassist Jason Roebke – a reliably punchy oft-times sideman of Chicago circles - and the indefatigable drummer Chris Corsano for a live date at Chicago’s Constellation from 2025. I cannot say there is much surprising here if you are familiar with Berman’s previous headline albums. That said, this is more of what this listener wants rather than simply more of the same. Berman clearly has a thing for bop, in its various forms, and maybe the title is even a nod to his appreciation of those who came before and inspired him. The songs on here start with a catchy head, or a few more plodding, smokey ones, and from there break down into spurs, knotty angles, and spindly striations. One could play this album for someone who thought Miles went too far when he went electric, or Coltrane with Ascension, and they would happily bob their head along with Roebke’s walking bass or Corsano’s steady patter behind Berman’s jumpy melodies. But restricting this to such a palatable bridge would miss the other point, which lies in the free form sections that, yes, are tied to the head but in a sensual way that deviates from its rhythm, tune, and key in favor of capturing, extending, and straining the intricacies of a spontaneous moment. Those sections are when Berman stretches into flutters, crackles, and bites, when Roebke leans into timbre, and Corsano eschews rhythm for sound. Those sections are limited; in this case I think for the better. That is not because trio cannot stretch out into the unknown. (Take the eighth cut, Scale, as an example of their exploratory chops.) Instead, it is because they do so within Berman’s bookending melodic confines that set the direction and mark the terminal point. And were those themes not inspired, this would fall flat. But they are and do not. For doubters, just listen to the wonderfully lonesome and wistful closer, Second Look, where Corsano’s brushes lay a soft-rain backdrop to Berman’s and Roebke’s melancholic dialog. Everybody Else’s Life, Too is much in the vein of a different Josh Berman Trio’s A Dance and a Hop (2015) and should be considered an expansion of that project. Again, you might well know what to expect if you have been following Berman already, but that does not make what you hear any less satisfying. Everybody Else’s Life, Too is available download from Bandcamp and a CD from a few choice independent music outlets. See the CvD website for more . items._cn_summary: 这是芝加哥爵士圈老将Josh Berman与贝斯手Jason Roebke、鼓手Chris Corsano合作的现场专辑，录制于2025年Constellation。这张作品延续了他此前《A Dance and a Hop》的路线，既包含以bop为根基的旋律主题，也深入自由即兴段落。歌曲通常从一个抓耳的或低沉烟雾感的主题出发，随后解构为棱角分明的即兴片段。评论指出，专辑中受限的自由即兴段落反而比无限制的探索更有效，因为旋律框架为自由段落提供了方向与终点。Roebke的扎实低音行走与Corsano的稳定节奏为Berman跳跃的旋律线提供支撑，而后者在即兴段落中则伸展为颤音、碎裂声与尖锐音色的实验。终曲《Second Look》展现了忧郁的对话质感。整体而言，这是一张在bop传统与自由即兴之间取得平衡的成熟作品。

items.excerpt: Label: ACT, 2026 Personnel - Emile Parisien: soprano saxophone; Yaron Herman: piano; Linda May Han Oh: bass; Prabhu Edouard: tabla, percussion, voice. French soprano saxophonist and composer Emile Parisien is an eclectic jazz practitioner with inestimable musical gifts that allow him to explore a whole universe of sound. items.body: Label: ACT, 2026 Personnel - Emile Parisien: soprano saxophone; Yaron Herman: piano; Linda May Han Oh: bass; Prabhu Edouard: tabla, percussion, voice. French soprano saxophonist and composer Emile Parisien is an eclectic jazz practitioner with inestimable musical gifts that allow him to explore a whole universe of sound. Parisien brings a glowing selection of tunes composed by himself, pianist and longtime collaborator Yaron Herman, and proficient bassist Linda May Han Oh, alongside two covers. Rounding out the quartet is tabla player and vocalist Prabhu Edouard, who helps establish an organically integrated framework for the leader’s world-fusion aesthetics. This group was formed after a memorable first performance in Paris. Floating opens with Georges Ivanovitch Gurdjieff and Thomas de Hartmann’s “ Asian Songs & Rhythms, No. 40 ”, a peaceful, spiritual tune that, combining Eastern modal traditions with Western classical sensibilities, slowly unfolds with a ternary feel. Parisien employs his intervallic expertise in vibrant phrasing, while Herman evokes distant, serene landscapes. The other cover on the album is Anouar Brahem’s “ Badhra ”—the fantastic opening track of his trio album Thimar—which scintillates with sophistication and enchantment. In the latter, Herman’s clarity of speech and objectivity pair well with the in-and-out lyricism of Parisien, while the duo’s co-written piece, “ Portal ”, keeps the rhythmic momentum going after a dynamic introduction centered on Edouard, who doubles on tabla and voice. Herman’ piano solo on this one is pure delight. On the other hand, Parisien’s “ Bonbon ” is filled with excitement and aligned with Middle Eastern traditions. Herman contributes five compositions of his own: the waltzing ballads “ Olive Branch ” and “ Ruth ”, with the latter acquiring a jazzier, Keith Jarrett-esque vibe before morphing into a more percussive passage over which Parisien’s soprano glides effortlessly; the playful and bluesy “ Nusrat ”; and the stop-and-go flow of “ El Toro ”, a showcase for Oh’s rhythmic adroitness. Sandwiched between the latter two tracks is the bassist’s “ As It Comes And As It Goes ”, a moment of reflection and an opportunity to hear her unaccompanied. According to the bandleader, this is music about peace, poetry, and love, and listeners should be able to feel its emotional appeal as well as the group’s ability to communicate through whatever musical language they choose to mix in. This forward-looking diversity is key, and Parisien’s fusion is not without an airily contemporary touch. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Asian Songs & Rhythms, No 40 ► 04 - Badhra ► 08 - Nusrat
items._cn_summary: 法国高音萨克斯演奏家Emile Parisien领衔的四重奏专辑，以东方模态传统与西方古典语汇的融合为核心框架。曲目来源多元，包括两位成员原创作品以及Gurdjieff和Brahem的改编曲。钢琴手Herman的作曲占据主体，旋律线条在爵士即兴与中东音阶之间游走；贝斯手Oh贡献独奏段落展示独立性；打击乐手Edouard以塔布拉与人声铺设节奏基底。整体编曲偏向抒情与冥想气质，萨克斯的音程跳跃在稳定的三拍子律动中展开，钢琴与贝斯构成对位支撑。专辑传递出和平、诗意与爱的主题，音乐语言不拘一格，融合深度足够但实验性相对克制，更多体现为调性与文化层面的交汇而非结构性的突破。
