items.body: Review by alainPP — NORTH SEA ECHOES, nothing new except for extending their first offering: heavier, more melancholic, more pervasive."A Time of Innocence and Purpose," with its bass and hypnotic, unsettling electro sample, is featured on LUNATIC SOUL. A beautiful ascent with Ray taking the lead, where things become much more interesting. A kind of GILDENLOW and pugnacious OSI hybrid, thanks to that captivating voice that makes all the difference. The ambient, intimate atmosphere makes you close your eyes and dream along to the edgy riff. "Enjoy The View" delves deeper into the electro-synthetic sound with its two-tone vocals and addictive instrumentation. The industrial riff, a sound effect on the thunderous breakdown, the keyboard undulating in a new dark-wave style. The magic works and endures with the energy of the invigorating chorus over the haunting verse, the haunting, dark outro. "Good Enough" features a crystalline, airy, stereo acoustic arpeggio reminiscent of the good old days. The raw, spoken-word vocals are laid over it, creating a country evening feel. The warm crescendo, with Ray as the sonic hero, evokes a dark Louisiana vibe with animals singing in the background: sublime and utterly simple, surfing on the atmospheric. "I'll Leave A Light On" kicks off with a fat riff, a melancholic nod to Katatonia. The pre-screamed vocals over the powerful sound, the chorus like something out of the mainstream era: the nostalgia is amplified by a punchy guitar solo bursting with notes. An added choir graces this track, which flows effortlessly, nothing new but well executed, finally on Fates Warning. "All Fall Away" boasts a bouncy bass beat. A dark, monolithic feel, redolent of Eurythmics in a heavy version, for this primal alternative drift. The guitar twists and turns, illuminating the space, the beat becomes oppressive, reminiscent of PARADISE LOST with Ray's voice, the chorus, then the beat abruptly stopping."Revenge," with its Wavy-esque guitar, surfs on the scales of THE CURE. This decadent rock descends to the realm of electro-pop, a softer DEPECHE MODE, Ray bribing his vocal cords. A repetitive, melancholic finale, far removed from prog rock. "Villains Or Saints" returns to mainstream, mainstream rock with its heavy melody, surfing once again on FATES WARNING. The haunting, synthetic rhythm builds and creates a heavy guitar space over the velvety keyboard. Ray conducts this masterful string piece, always effortless yet captivating, this timeless ballad. "What Is And What Was What," with its dark, ambient, mysterious intro and that wind that seems to come from nowhere. Vocals over a guitar arpeggio, choir over organ, hairs shiver. The bass resonates, clears the speakers, the pleasure of having this vibrant, body-piercing sound, like an arrow piercing your heart. "All That Comes After" returns to edgy rock, energized by its catchy melody. A B-side track that doesn't offer anything new, however, except perhaps to test the stereo image on the atmospheric drift. This melodic sound takes you back to the previous millennium. "How To Cast A Shadow" concludes, the new-wave vibe with its heady keyboard, as fat as the 'metroganic' drums, Ray weaving through this dark, hybrid, alternative slow jam. The mantra-like latency for dancing, swaying with his wife, the guitar both melancholic and slide-like. The feeling of navigating a bayou. A heavy guitar solo, the sound that makes you headbang, the refrain of 80s hard rock bands, I'm sucked into this musical spiral. The finale features Ray clinging to the primal synth, shh... Silence remains a constant presence throughout the album, with its enveloping notes.NORTH SEA ECHOES pushes their identity further with a heavy, dark approach, evolving with the addition of electronic elements to delve into the ghosts of the past, temptation, and reflection. (3.75)
items._genre: crossover prog / darkwave / industrial / alternative rock / electro-synthetic
items._cn_summary: North Sea Echoes 的第二张专辑延续了首作的整体方向，质感上更加沉重、忧郁且渗透性强。乐评提及与 Lunatic Soul、OSI、Katatonia、Paradise Lost、Depeche Mode、The Cure 等乐队的相似性，说明作品在跨界融合上有明确追求。电声合成元素与暗潮律动贯穿全作，主唱 Ray 的声线是核心粘合剂，将工业 riff、新浪潮旋律与前卫摇滚结构串联。多首曲目以电吉他琶音、合成器铺底和教堂般合唱营造氛围，如"What Is And What Was What"和"Good Enough"的对比展现出从空灵原声到阴郁工业的宽广音域。整体制作精良，但乐评也指出部分曲目缺乏新意，停留在既有风格的安全区域。对暗潮、电子合成与前卫摇滚交界地带感兴趣的听众值得一听。

items.body: Am I capable of writing about music without referencing Eurovision? I guess not, especially if the band in question legitimately competed in a recent edition of my beloved song contest. By charming over 76,000 voters with an atmospheric blend of Nordic folk rock, Gåte won the 62nd Melodi Grand Prix, subsequently leading to their appearance at the Eurovision Song Contest 2024, representing Norway. Despite moving on from their allotted semifinal, the group placed dead last amongst the twenty-five finalists. The chaotic performance of their song "Ulveham" didn't impress international audiences or the professional jury, but it sure as hell made an impact on one American Eurofan, and the consensus among hardcore watchers is that Gåte was brutally robbed. After their undeserved flop, Gåte retreated to the forests of Norway for two years, finally reemerging with Sigil—a grander full-length to rekindle the sylvan aura they condensed and presented to over a hundred million people in just three minutes. I like to think of Gåte like a wreath. The center is vocalist Gunnhild Sundli. Her vocalizations—whether singing or chanting—have an unmistakable inflection that drifts over each piece with both tenderness and command. When she dips down into her lower register, the atmosphere turns foggy, but when Sundli lifts her tones high she effortlessly clears the fog to reveal a lively forest. Her technique is perfect for this genre of folk rock, and probably the main reason for Gåte's longevity as a band. Adorning the surrounding area of the wreath are class-act musicians wielding an assortment of traditional instruments. Right-hand man Magnus Børmark plays guitar but also the Swedish nyckelharpa, drummer Jon Even Schärer handles all sorts of percussion, as well as a mouth harp, and Arent Todal tackles various stringed instruments. Further adding to the wreath (specifically to Sigil) is the legion of session artists. I may not be able to quickly discern Marit Aspås's cello from Olav Luksengård Mjelva's hardanger fiddle, but these instruments are key in creating the record's environment. Don't expect these instruments to shred at full capacity. Sigil is a slow burner, churning atmospheres with crescendos rather than jamming out. Although the ambiances Gåte builds are splendid, not a single song runs over five minutes long. This hinders what these ten songs could be. The best pieces like "Strandvaskar" pull off heavy-hitting, successful climaxes, while others like "Nokon" spend too much time creating the liftoff for a climax. I adore the slow songs, especially the pairing of ballads ending the album, and now that the band is on a bigger label, a more digestible approach to their wizardry is expected. But if Gåte's mission is to conjure grand images of Nordic myths and legends, packing it all into three-minute chunks probably isn't the right way to go about it. Sigil by Gåte

items.body: Amamere come from Cape Coast, the Fante fishing port where Ebo Taylor and C.K. Mann were born, and they play highlife the way Ghana’s guitar bands played it in the 1970s. Eric Asiedu Agyekum‘s lead guitar sits out front, tenor sax and trumpet play over the top, and behind the kit is Rim Akandoh Jnr, who spent the late 2010s drumming for Taylor. Their live take on “Kokonsani”, the opening track of the 2025 debut Man Shall Be Free on Afro Urban Project, was filmed at Afrika Festival Hertme in the Netherlands on 4 July, during the eight-piece’s first tour outside Ghana. Dominic Ansah plays Ga kpanlogo drums and congas under the kit, and the trumpet belongs to Emmanuel Adjei, grandson of Osibisa‘s Mac Tontoh. Akandoh Jnr’s father, Rim Akandoh, played in Mann’s band before leading the Prince Sparrows Band. Much of the album reworks his songs alongside osode, the fishing-community music Mann electrified, while “Kokonsani”, Twi for a gossip, carries the son’s own lyric. Hear the studio cut of “Kokonsani” HERE and order Man Shall Be Free via THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Amamere – Kokonsani appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Kommission Z80 is a Swedish duo that, following a debut album released on Electric Underground Records, is now self-releasing its second opus. I don’t recall ever hearing anything by them before, but these 13 tracks provide a clear picture of the duo’s musical identity. Their primary influences clearly lie within the realm of old-school EBM—specifically the kind of EBM characterized by thoughtful composition and well-crafted arrangements. The vocals, and indeed some of the tracks, remind me somewhat of Portion Control, while other songs reveal traces of Skinny Puppy’s influence. One track even feels like a nod to Front 242. It should be noted that these are all bands with highly distinctive sounds and complex structures. Kommission Z80 doesn’t quite reach that level yet; they would benefit from improving some technical aspects, particularly the mixing and recording. Nevertheless, there is undeniable potential here. Several strong tracks are waiting to be discovered, and the latter part of the album, in particular, features some very cool songs. Kommission Z80 is a name that true EBM enthusiasts should remember. (Rating:7). Listen to “Here Comes The Consequences”: Here Comes The Consequences by Kommission Z80 About Kommission Z80 Kommission Z80 is a Swedish duo from Borås formed by Erik Holmberg and Fredrich Legnemark, working in an old-school EBM style. The project’s debut single “Empire” arrived in 2024 through Electric Underground Records, followed by the debut album “Hegemony” and the “Reasonable Conclusions” EP in 2025. “Sic Semper Tyrannis” is the duo’s self-released 2026 follow-up.
items._cn_summary: 瑞典二人组Kommission Z80的第二张专辑延续了老派EBM路线，13首曲目展现出对Portion Control、Skinny Puppy和Front 242等经典工业电子乐队的致敬与继承。制作上偏向严谨的编曲与结构安排，人声处理带有冷峻的工业感，部分曲目融入了更复杂的层次与律动变化。不过评论指出混音与录音技术仍有提升空间，与前辈的标志性声音和复杂结构相比尚有距离。专辑后半部分集中呈现了若干质量突出的作品，整体虽有潜力，但在声音辨识度与技术完成度上尚未完全成熟。适合深耕EBM场景的听众聆听，作品在传统类型框架内提供了一定的新鲜感。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以中提琴、管风琴、击弦古钢琴和钢琴为核心乐器，辅以鼓、贝斯和合成器，呈现即兴式的一次性录音美学。乐评着重分析了几首作品的技法与气质：约翰·克莱尔诗作配以持续低音铺垫的旋律线，带有超越尘世的宗教感；标题曲以中世纪圣咏风格开篇，钢琴主导的级进旋律缓慢展开，成为专辑情感支点；另一首则取材于古老民歌语汇，呼应跨越时空的怀旧情绪。整张专辑是Cotton为2024年末去世的父亲所作的纪念之作，丧失、眷恋与告别交织于各曲目之间，光与暗的情绪不断交替。音乐难以归类，融合民谣、前卫与即兴元素，既有冥想式的静谧，又有缓慢累积的张力，挑战听众同时给予深层满足。

A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组的首张数字EP，五首曲目以北欧传统民谣为底色。主唱Mia Guldhammer嗓音极具说服力与感染力，是乐评重点关注的对象。音乐家们各自带入不同的视角重新诠释传统素材，仅有一首原创作品出自成员Morten Musicus之手。器乐配置丰富多样：口簧与风笛在《Nordgård》中形成强劲的推进力，洋琴（cimbalom）为传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》铺陈出精致的背景层次，口簧、长笛与弦乐交织的终曲《Ormsö》呈现出令人兴奋的离调与不平衡质感。整体笼罩着古老、粗糙的氛围，乐队虽初登场却显得成熟而老练，为北欧民谣场景注入新鲜活力。

items._cn_summary: A Certain Ratio 重新发行了1982年的《The Joy of Sextet》和1986年的《Force Majeure》两张专辑。乐评指出乐队近年高产，但此次转向档案再版工作，提出新作可能枯竭的担忧。实际发行的是两张方式截然不同的伴侣专辑，分别对应各自的周年纪念节点，配有全新混音与曲目排列，并附带一些意外曲目。这些重新整理的版本为曼彻斯特后朋克的老乐迷提供了回顾乐队早期编曲与制作脉络的机会，也展示了他们融合放克元素与后朋克冷峻律动的独特美学。对该用户而言，后朋克与暗潮口味有交集，但缺乏明显的实验或电子跨界维度，整体吸引力中等。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Uncompromising art rock for a fresh sound, minimalist and captivating alternative electro-prog."My Blistering Mind" boasts a distinctive sound, phrased vocals, and electronic, synth-heavy orchestration reminiscent of Porcupine Tree. A final mantra-like repetition of the gentle chorus shifts between pop, cold wave, and Bowie-esque dance-pop-rock, all set to poignant lyrics about mental fragility. "The Mandatory Prize" features a synthetic riff on electric piano, a long, melancholic, and pervasive melody set to lyrics by Dick, with a sound reminiscent of Steve Wilson. Malcolm's voice is ever-present, pale, cold, and robotic, mirroring the synth pads in a new prog style. But that riff is truly gut-wrenching. "Never Really Felt Like Home," with its ambient, hypnotic, and contemplative intro, and Kathryn's deep flute, is a symbol of tranquility. The piccolo allows for a drift into a cinematic-melancholic space where the low guitar solo amplifies this beatific, solemn instrumental. "Smile, Smile, Smile," already seen on the EP, has a haunting metronomic sound on the vibrating bass, the keyboard unfolding, flirting with Esth�sie, the addictive vocals leading to saturation. An electronic Wilson, like his side project No-Man. A stressful, redundant finale leading to musical madness through its endless repetition, the lyrics cruelly explaining this moment of schizoid disarray. "Intermission," as its name suggests, is an instrumental on bass and drums with a jazzy piano, a way of dreaming about the evolution of jazz today. The ensuing Mellotron chills the ears before the colorful piano nods to the works of Joe Jackson."Parallel Lives," with its hushed vocals and contemplative ballad-like feel, sees Kathryn's guitar work on the chorus amplify its solemnity. The effective rhythmic foundation drives this lament, reminiscent of Springsteen's "Streets of Philadelphia." The eponymous track plunges into the depths of Wavy's pop. "Eversion," one of the longer pieces, meanders with lyrics reminiscent of Kate Bush, its orchestration blending neoclassical, synth, and electronic elements, inspired by Steve Wilson. A piano and synth interlude precedes the electric return and Malcolm's vocals, sly, dark, and haughty. The guitar solo brightens the ear, and the sound returns with hypnotic, syncopated percussion, amplifying the progressive, schizophrenic feel. "Pretty Blue Fox" opens with a modern, electro-synth feel, reminiscent of Tangerine Dream in the 70s. It's a blend of electro and prog, with a satisfying mid-section, scraping away at the repetitive sounds of Philip Glass for a restrained, immersive, orgasmic finale ? pure bliss. "Just Another Thing" returns to new prog rock with its piercing, guttural vocals; you'll want to try these breathless vocalizations yourself. There's a hint of Bowie, a sound reminiscent of Simple Minds, a dynamic track with a neo-Marillion-esque keyboard solo, recounting Malcolm's retinal mishaps. "Dropping The Mask" is another instrumental with an electrified, upbeat tempo and bouncy keyboard, a nod to Tangerine Dream in the 80s ? groovy, energetic, and catchy. "Just Hold On (Pts 1 & 2)" opens with a religious, elegiac intro, the soaring choir drifting into hyperspace?a fitting way to escape this groundbreaking album. A striking mix of languid atmosphere and archaic feel, thanks to a guitar emerging from a cloud of Olympus, the solo spreading to the heavens. Malcolm finally appears on this melting synth, the drums merely controlling the rhythm. A solemn ambiance is created by the double bass, the deep vocals, the ephemeral piano, and the final, melancholic guitar outro, a meditative and hopeful finale. A truly beautiful and contemplative ending. "My Blistering Mind," in a shorter, perhaps faster version, and "The Mandatory Prize" are released as radio edits, destined for the airwaves of a better world.HATS OFF GENTLEMEN IT'S ADEQUATE blends vocal and purely instrumental tracks, delivering electronic art-rock with contemporary classical touches. A modern progressive rock sound for the new millennium. (4.5)
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑呈现出折衷主义的前卫摇滚面貌，融合电子合成器编排与简约艺术摇滚结构。作品频繁借鉴Porcupine Tree和Steven Wilson式的冷峻合成器美学，辅以Bowie式的舞曲流行色彩、Kate Bush式的神经质人声以及Tangerine Dream式的电子氛围。长笛与短笛的运用增添了电影化的忧郁空间，爵士钢琴间奏与Mellotron织体穿插其中。歌词聚焦精神脆弱与人格分裂的主题，旋律以冥想式重复和催眠节奏推进，营造出沉思而略带不安的聆听体验。整体制作强调合成器音色与人声的冷调互动，吉他独奏作为情绪释放点出现，是一张概念连贯但风格取向上较为依赖前辈影子的crossover prog作品。

items.body: Black Tape For A Blue Girl and Projekt Records reissue “The Rope” on October 2, presenting the 1986 debut album in a limited edition that pairs the original mix, remastered, with a new 2026 mix by Sam Rosenthal for its 40th anniversary. The 2LP edition is limited to 300 copies on 140-gram vinyl, with LP1 pressed on baby blue vinyl with black splatters and LP2 on transparent blue vinyl with white splatters. A 2CD digipak edition adds seven bonus tracks. Both formats are released via Projekt Records. “The Rope” is Black Tape For A Blue Girl’s debut album, the project Sam Rosenthal built around his songwriting and electronics, with Oscar Herrera on vocals. Each format includes the full 12-track album twice: the original 1986 mix, remastered, and the new 2026 mix. Martin Bowes of Attrition handled the mastering. The 2LP package adds a 16-page lyric and memorabilia fanzine insert plus a sticker; the 2CD edition comes in a 6-panel digipak with a 4-panel photo insert and sticker. The original 1986 tracklist runs: “memory, uncaring friend”, “hide in yourself”, “within these walls”, “the holy terrors”, “end”, “seven days til sunrise”, “the rope”, “the few remaining threads”, “the lingering flicker”, “slow blur”, “the floor was hard but home” and “we return”. The 2CD edition adds seven bonus tracks exclusive to that format: “the lingering flicker (first draft)”, “within these walls (early mix with clarinet)”, “the holy terrors (long)”, “second dream”, “the lingering flicker (isolated violins)”, “within these walls (short with violins)” and “memory, uncaring friend (remix intro)”. Sam Rosenthal on writing ‘The Rope’ Rosenthal, who also founded Projekt Records, described the circumstances that produced the album: “In November ’85, following two years of recording instrumental electronic music, I invited Oscar Herrera to sing two songs on my ISLANDS cassette. A few months later in February of ’86 I left Florida for college in Orange, California. I was 20 years old, feeling isolated, lonely, missing friends back home. In my dorm room that spring I used the school’s Fostex 250 4-track cassette portastudio to record songs with my lyrics and melodies. Writing words for Oscar to sing over my ethereal and ambient music helped me explore those angsty and tangled feelings. The Rope is half vocal and half instrumental. It’s all quite minimal, yet it’s an album listeners still mention as a favorite. Capturing the confusion and darkness I felt at that time remains valid; new listeners connect with it today. I never would have expected that 40 years later The Rope would be listened to and appreciated by new generations. It’s really nice knowing those feelings are timeless, and the music has a place in people’s lives.” Uncut included “The Rope” in its “200 Greatest Goth Albums” feature, describing it as: “The vehicle for the more electronic songwriting of Projekt Records’ founder Sam Rosenthal, brought to life by singer Oscar Herrera’s arch delivery. BTFABG spun a unique thread of ambient darkwave, neoclassical exoticism and dark cabaret on their relatively bare-boned and lo-fi debut album.” The Rope (40th) by Black Tape For A Blue Girl About Black Tape For A Blue Girl Black Tape For A Blue Girl is the project Sam Rosenthal formed in 1986, built around his own songwriting and electronics and centered from the start on the pairing of his instrumental, ambient compositions with vocalists singing his lyrics. “The Rope”, released that year on Projekt Records, the label Rosenthal founded, introduced Oscar Herrera as vocalist alongside contributions from Allan Kraut, Kim Prior, Adam Buhler, Candy Sherlock and Lara Radford. The project’s discography continued through “Mesmerized by the Sirens” (1987), “Ashes in the Brittle Air” (1989), “A Chaos of Desire” (1991), “This Lush Garden Within” (1993), “Remnants of a Deeper Purity” (1996), “As One Aflame Laid Bare by Desire” (1999), “The Scavenger Bride” (2002), “Halo Star” (2004), “10 Neurotics” (2009), “Tenderotics” (2013), “These Fleeting Moments” (2016), “To Touch the Milky Way” (2018) and “The Cleft Serpent” (2021). Projekt has revisited several of these titles as anniversary reissues in recent years, including “The Cleft Serpent” and “Ashes in the Brittle Air” on vinyl, “Mesmerized by the Sirens” on vinyl and double CD, and “As One Aflame Laid Bare by Desire” and “Remnants of a Deeper Purity” in their own anniversary editions. Rosenthal has also continued to release music outside the project, including ambient and drone recordings under his own name. The 40th anniversary edition of “The Rope” extends that reissue campaign to the album that started it, presenting Herrera’s original vocal performances and Rosenthal’s 1986 arrangements alongside his 2026 revisiting of the same material.
items._cn_summary: Black Tape For A Blue Girl由Sam Rosenthal于1986年以Fostex 4-track卡带录音机在大学宿舍完成首张专辑，以极简的电子氛围编制搭配Oscar Herrera的人声，捕捉了创作者初入大学时的孤独、纠结与黑暗情绪。专辑半数为器乐、半数为人声曲目，在当时以ambient和ethereal元素为基础构建出暗潮美学的雏形。40周年再版由Projekt Records发行，提供原始混音与2026新混音双版本，限量2LP采用蓝色彩胶压制，2CD版额外收录七首稀有版本和早期混音。Martin Bowes负责母带处理，发行设计附歌词册与周边。整体定位偏向darkwave与ethereal wave交叉领域，属于小众独立厂牌的复古再版企划，对暗潮与氛围电子爱好者具备收藏价值。

items.body: Room of Wires, the UK industrial/electronic duo of two producers who both go by Andrew, released the single “Skin weevil” on September 18, 2026, self-released on Bandcamp. The two-track release pairs the title track with “Do not leave a message” and arrives while the duo works on a new album. Skin weevil by Room of Wires Room of Wires bring an industrial and electronic sound that mixes hard-hitting rhythm programming with the duo’s usual dark ambient textures and field recordings. Both tracks on “Skin weevil” were written and produced by Room of Wires; the cover artwork is by the duo as well, with performance for camera by Fenia Kotsopoulou and photography by Daz Disley. Room of Wires’ ‘Skin weevil’ single The duo has not met in person: one member works with hardware and a tangle of physical wires, the other in software and virtual cables, sharing ideas and sounds over the internet. That process has produced “Skin weevil” as a standalone two-track single rather than part of a longer EP or album, released independently while the pair continue work on their next full-length. No further tracks or release date for that album have been announced. About Room of Wires Room of Wires is a UK industrial/electronic duo of two producers, both named Andrew, who write and record without ever having met, exchanging sounds and ideas remotely. Their debut EP, “Asylum sneaker”, appeared on Section27 in August 2014, followed by the Bandcamp-only “Dead skins” EP in November 2015, “Used as a runner” on Section27 in June 2016, “Black medicine” on Section27 in June 2017, and the remix-featuring “Mastakink” EP, self-released in October 2017. Their debut album, “White transit”, followed in November 2018, and the mini-LP “Test subject” arrived in October 2019. Room of Wires signed to the German label ant-zen for the albums “Plague of people” (April 2021) and “Welcome to the end game” (February 2023), releasing the “Fever switch” EP on Rednetic in October 2021 in between. Further self-released EPs followed with “Floodplains” (November 2023) and the album “If no other means are effective” in December 2025, the duo’s first full-length in close to three years. Alongside their own catalogue, Room of Wires record collaborative material as DasF and Cave like carving, and have contributed remixes and tracks to releases by Ah Cama-Sotz, Flint Glass, 4T Thieves and other acts. “Skin weevil” is their first new material since 2025’s “If no other means are effective”, released as the pair continue work on a new Room of Wires album.
items._cn_summary: Room of Wires 是一支由两位同名为 Andrew 的英国制作人组成的工业/电子二人组，两人从未线下见面，分别通过硬件与软件远程合作完成创作。此次新单曲《Skin weevil》于2026年9月以自发行方式登陆Bandcamp，包含标题曲与《Do not leave a message》两首作品，延续了硬核节奏编程与暗氛围纹理、现场录音相结合的路线。文章详细梳理了乐队自2014年以来的厂牌合作脉络，包括Section27、ant-zen与Rednetic等小众厂牌经历，体现出地下场景的长期积累。作为纯新闻性质发布通告，文章未对音乐本身进行深入评析或批评性探讨，缺乏对声音设计、作曲手法或艺术定位的实质性评论，信息深度有限。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'Tellurian' is the second studio album from Swedish progressive metal band Soen, a relatively newact that features ex-Opeth drummer Martin Lopez alongside vocalist Joel Ekel�f and guitarist JoakimPlatbarzdis, whose sound strongly resembles fellow progressive acts Tool and Leprous, and to alesser extent the alternative metal played by System of a Down and Katatonia. Similarly to theirdebut album 'Cognitive', but with a greater sense of identity, this 2014 release offers a crisp andcontemporary atmospheric progressive metal sound that features a fine balance between technicallyacute guitar riffs and soothing instrumental liquidity that projects itself in the form ofsyncopated rhythms and dense grooves. There is a bit of experimentation going on as well,particularly in the rhythm section, as drummer Martin Lopez lays down some diverse and delightfulgrooves, perhaps channeling his inner Danny Carey. The vocals represent another interesting part ofthis record, as the delivery of Joel Ekel�f is warm and emotive, definitely befitting the etherealstyle of rock that prevails on 'Tellurian'. There is a certain aspect of the album that is touchingand melancholic, while the record itself is consistent and well-structured, with strong entries like'Tabula Rasa', 'Pluton' and 'Void' beautifully depicting Soen's stylistic leanings. At the sametime, some tracks feel drawn out and monotonous, with a lightweight, atmospheric tone that ismaintained for the entire duration of the songs, as heard on 'The Words' or 'The Other's Fall'. Thiscompletely takes away their compositional edge, and it also diminishes the appeal of the strongertracks. Therefore, 'Tellurian' is hardly a groundbreaking prog metal masterpiece; it is more of adriven and consistent collection of songs, which salvages the weaker moments, and presents Soen as agroup searching for a recognizable sound.
items._cn_summary: Soen 的第二张专辑以技术犀利的吉他riff与流畅的器乐编排构建氛围化前卫金属，在切分节奏与密集律动之间寻找平衡。鼓手 Martin Lopez 来自 Opeth，他在节奏部分展现了多样化且充满实验性的处理方式，被比作 Danny Carey 式的复杂律动。主唱 Joel Ekelöf 的演绎温暖且情感丰沛，与专辑弥漫的飘渺气质契合。专辑呈现出忧郁与哀伤的基调，整体结构连贯，《Tabula Rasa》《Pluton》《Void》等曲目代表乐队风格的核心倾向。然而部分曲目如《The Words》《The Other's Fall》被认为过于冗长单调，轻飘的氛围贯穿始终削弱了作曲锋芒。整体而言，这并非颠覆性的前卫金属杰作，而是一张驱动力稳定且一致性较强的作品集，展现了乐队在塑造辨识度道路上的探索。

items._cn_summary: 本篇乐评以"记忆与未来的回响"为线索，串联三位艺术家的作品。开篇聚焦挪威裔美国声音艺术家 John Derek Bishop 与 Khaled Habeeb 的专辑《Ekkofremtit》，专辑标题在挪威语中意为"回声未来"，暗示其创作核心在于探索记忆如何与当下互动并塑造未来。Bishop 作为声音艺术家，其作品可能涉及田野录音、声音拼贴与环境声景等实验手法。乐评还提及 Samuel Blaser 与 Rymden 的作品，但正文截断，仅留下开篇引言。由于内容严重不足，无法获取具体音乐技法、制作细节或艺术立场的深入讨论，只能依据标题与简介推测其偏向实验性、跨界融合方向。整体而言，这是一篇面向小众读者的前瞻乐评，但信息密度极低，参考价值有限。

items._cn_summary: 本文为Jazz Journal杂志1966年9月刊关于Roland Kirk专辑《Slightly Latin》的旧文转载回顾。Steve Voce在六十年前的评论中指出，Kirk的这张专辑相较当时大多数前卫爵士作品，在保持现代感的同时呈现出更强的内在连贯性。专辑以拉丁爵士为切入点，将加勒比海与南美节奏元素融入Kirk标志性的多支管乐器同吹演奏（manzello、tenor sax、stritch等）中。整体定位介于传统拉丁爵士与早期前卫爵士探索之间，既保留了摇摆感与旋律骨架，又在和声与编制上展现了实验意识。原文为杂志节选片段，内容极为简短，缺乏对具体曲目编排、录音细节或演奏技法的深入分析，仅提供了一句话式的整体印象评价，信息量有限。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025
items.label: Hudson Records
items._genre: folk / contemporary classical / ambient sound design
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于苏格兰皇家植物园驻留项目，以园中最古老的棕榈树为核心展开叙事。钢琴与人声为主体，配合精心设计的声景，构筑出兼具庄严感与亲密感的氛围。歌词与音乐中反复出现的旋律段落如同锚点，引导听众进入一段关于自然、历史与时间的旅程。终曲揭示了树种身份的两百年误认，子孙幼苗将在前辈曾经矗立之处继续生长，乐评认为这为整部作品赋予了希望与轮回的意味。整体而言，这是将民谣根基与当代古典气质结合的跨界作品，声景手法为传统人声钢琴配置带来层次，但音乐语言本身并不偏向实验或前卫。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)
items.label: Buda Musique
items._genre: bal-musette / French chanson / ragtime / jug band / eclectic folk
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dominique Cravic与地下漫画家Robert Crumb合作的Les Primitifs du futur系列的第五张作品。整体风格无法简单归类，像是创作者从阁楼中翻出大量78转唱片重新编排，用手风琴、萨克斯、班卓琴、尤克里里、木锯、特雷门琴等各式乐器录制了27首短曲。音乐以法国bal-musette为基底，融合了拉格泰姆、爵士乐、法国香颂以及skiffle等元素。Cravic的演唱方式类似日常化的Maurice Chevalier，半说半唱。曲目涵盖1925年老歌Ukulele Lady的重新演绎，以及向2020年去世的法国抵抗运动女歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的作品。乐评将其与Dan Hicks & His Hot Licks相比，认为这是一群年逾七旬的严肃音乐家以热情与匠心重新激活被遗忘的音乐风格。专辑在自身的小角落里散发着独特光芒。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�
items.label: Mig
items._genre: New Orleans R&B / funk / Mardi Gras revue
items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑录制于1999年莱茵河畔洛勒莱露天剧场，呈现了Dr. John以新奥尔良传统为核心的舞台表演。演出以四人编制乐队为支撑，涵盖新奥尔良经典如《Iko, Iko》，融合放克节奏的《Qualified》，以及带有巫毒仪式色彩与迷幻吉他独奏的《I Walk on Guilded Splinters》。曲目编排兼顾个人代表作《Sweet Home New Orleans》与向Duke Ellington致敬的作品，并以《Big Chief》收束，整体呈现为一场多元风格交融的狂欢节式回顾演出。乐评指出其表演跨越语言与文化障碍，展现了音乐的普遍感染力，但内容偏向传统新奥尔良节奏布鲁斯与放克路线，虽有世界音乐元素，与实验或前卫领域的关联有限。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是声音记录者Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区枪支暴力幸存者社区前廊完成的实地录音集。二十五位年龄从十七岁到六十七岁的参与者讲述各自与枪支暴力的遭遇，内容多为口述证词，夹杂少量即兴说唱。录音地点位于机场航线下方，背景音包括野猫走动和祖母对蚊虫的提醒。编辑放弃了传统乐评形式，直接引用录音师的简短评述与原始声迹。项目收益将捐赠给Cure Violence Global。整张专辑更接近社会听觉文献与田野录音艺术，而非音乐创作，与实验音乐领域的田野录音传统有一定关联，但在音乐性上较为薄弱。

items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非原创乐评，而是来自Freq的近期评论汇总，包含两条简短介绍。其一涉及The Necks乐队的现场演出，三位音乐家以钢琴、贝斯和鼓进行长篇即兴演奏，延续了自由爵士与即兴音乐的传统；其二介绍Theory of Ghosts的EP3，将编程打击乐、采样、电子音效与键盘相结合，融入暗黑合成器流行与室内乐元素。从口味匹配度看，两组艺人分别覆盖了学院派自由爵士与电子实验两个方向，与用户偏好高度契合。然而文章内容过于简短，仅为转载性质的信息摘录，缺乏对音乐细节、演奏技法或艺术价值的深入分析，无法提供足够的参考价值。整体而言，信息密度不足，难以据此判断作品的真正水准。

items.body: Ahead of a comprehensive box set of live recordings, Richard Foster considers the 'other' Joy Division that barely gets mentioned; the live powerhouse that motored its way across Britain and Europe Joy Division live by Martin O'Neill As the old line goes, we tell ourselves stories in order to live. Sometimes we do this speculatively, through other people’s lives. This kind of speculation also drives the discourse around Joy Division’s brief and tragic history. A reason to look anew at this well-thumbed tale is the release of an official collection of live audio and video recordings - with unreleased, often brilliant material. It has a canny name: Eternal (Live). The music and video is accompanied by epoch-defining images from the celebrated band photographers,... items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — Once again fabulously illustrated by Annette Appleton in a captivating pictorial style?part na�ve, part naturalistic, and slightly dreamlike?*Estanyo Nord* is the last album by the English duo The Light Afternoon, aka Steve Newland, the ultra-perfectionist multi-instrumentalist, and Annette Appleton, the singer-illustrator with a shy, fairy-like voice. To illustrate the cover of *Estanyo Nord* and the inside poster, Annette was determined to depict the Panorama house and its surroundings as a veritable Garden of Eden, with a profusion of very real animals?mostly birds and cats, but also dogs and a gecko?in a visionary and imaginative style that makes this miraculous bestiary seem surreal and symbolic.The album tells the story of this exotic miniature Walden, a little lost paradise, just a stone's throw from the road and a short walk from the sea, and of its inhabitants? whether human (Ana Cirema and all the other souls of the household) or non-human?mostly cats ("Our Time In The Tin North")?who thrived in Panorama under a dark velvet sky streaked with shooting stars. Conceptually and structurally, *Estanyo Nord* is divided into two distinct parts ("Part One: Anacirema," "Part Two: Estanyo Nord"), like the two sides of a vinyl record, each consisting of four tracks, 4 or 5 minutes per track, for a total running time of 38 minutes?thus respecting the spirit and constraints of vinyl records from their heyday. All of this is significant because *Estanyo Nord* draws heavily on the past?from nostalgic memories of Steve and Annette's personal histories to the musical past of everyone who lived through the '80s to the fullest, in a way that was deceptively carefree yet truly full of hope, filled with both certainties and doubts. " "I don't know what makes me happy, I just know what makes me sad, I do my best to remember all the things that make me glad" ("All Of These Things," luminous memories of Malta, France, and Spain) "Musically, Estanyo Nord is very different from our previous album because Steve didn't want to make *The History of Mr. Puffin Man?The Sequel*" (dixit Annette). One couldn't put it better. As dynamic and assertive as the previous album was languid, gentle, and undulating, *Estanyo Nord* has categorically moved away from the dark symphonic prog of La Renaissance or Dead Can Dance, with the instrumental sounds and rhythmic programming here very clearly oriented toward synth-pop. But both albums share the same melancholy and a highly cinematic approach to music, with subtle touches of modulation and tense minor chords. This is particularly evident from the very start of "Wide Open Highway Road Movie," with its *Midnight Express*-like atmosphere, its sharp guitar chords and solos set against highway rhythms, and its synths so distinctly '80s that you can almost hear that faint vintage hiss that followed each synth note, following the strange hum of the electric current that had set them vibrating. With a slower sequenced tempo, "The Girl from Panorama" is more reminiscent of Kraftwerk or the early Human League. Meanwhile, the more high-energy "Anacirema" and "Estanyo Nord"?true hit potential?blend new wave rock and dance music much as New Order did a few years ago. Those who enjoyed the symphonic harmonies of *The History Of Mr Puffin Man* might prefer "The Paradero" and "All of These Things," with their delicate, haunting melodies, piano arpeggios, mysterious or commanding synths, subtle vocal arrangements, and that guitar that reminds me of Pulsar's *Gorlitz* (1989) in a slightly decadent, fin-de-si�cle (20th-century) atmosphere that evokes Bowie's legendary and unconventional *Low*. This European atmosphere is present with even more tenderness and romanticism on the slow "Watching the Perseids," a small, classically influenced pocket symphony. "Our Time in the Tin North" is closer to the atmospheric post-prog of Soup or North Atlantic Oscillation or the dreamy electronica of Tangerine Dream's latest albums, which should appeal to most of us. But regardless of our musical preferences and how open-minded we are in this regard, it would be a shame to miss this precious opportunity to own such an artistic work?one that is as valuable for its visual presentation as for its musical content. At first glance, it may seem relatively far removed from the usual canons of progressive rock, but ultimately, it is as universal as beauty itself.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张概念结构分明的专辑，以黑胶唱片A/B面逻辑划分为两部分，共八首曲目。音乐上从早期交响前卫风格明显转向合成器流行方向，'80年代合成器音色贯穿始终，尖锐的吉他和弦与公路节奏形成电影化叙事感。与前作相比，摒弃了暗色调交响前卫和Dead Can Dance式的阴郁氛围，转而拥抱明亮、动态且具怀旧感的合成器流行。专辑围绕一处名为Panorama的居所展开叙事，描绘了人与猫鸟共存的微型乌托邦主题，并以丰富的手绘插画作为视觉延伸。整体上哀愁情绪仍在，但音乐语汇明显大众化，更靠近80年代合成器流行与公路电影配乐的质感。

items.body: Review by toroddreincarnated — The second album from this band from Norway.The band was a duo with a line-up of double bass, bass, guitars, keyboards, concertina, effects andvocals.A number of guests added drums, violins, strings and trumpet.This is the follow-up album to their 2024 debut album Bridge Of Sighs from 2024. An album I reviewedback in April 2024 in # 3 of my blog The Sound Of Fighting Cats. I gave it a three stars review.Lullabies for the Marooned clocks in at three quarters of an hour.The music here is art-rock.The band, I mean duo, has retreated from the more rocking soundscape on their debut album into amuch more intimate, softly spoken and refined soundscape on their new album, the follow-up album.Early Genesis, Procol Harum, Sylvan, Talk Talk and Peter Hammill are good references here. There areeven some Steve Hogarth era Marillion lurking around in their music too. There is a blend of acoustic and electric instruments here, including guitars. The strings is addinga lot of colours and are complementing the great vocals.This is an album where a piece of music crosses over to becoming an artwork. The result is a great album and one of this year's better albums from Norway, the new powerhouse inart-rock and prog rock. 4 stars

items._cn_summary: 挪威双人组合的第二张专辑，从首张较为摇滚化的风格转向更为内敛、柔和的氛围。专辑以低音提琴、贝斯、吉他、键盘、手风琴及人声为核心，辅以小提琴、弦乐和号角的客串编制，将原声与电声乐器融合，弦乐为出色的人声增添丰富色彩。整体音乐呈现出从乐章向艺术作品跨越的特质，参考对象涵盖早期Genesis、Procol Harum、Sylvan、Talk Talk、Peter Hammill及Steve Hogarth时期的Marillion，属于艺术摇滚与跨界前卫的范畴。评论给予四星评价，认为是挪威年度佳作之一。

items.body: Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart reissue the 2xCD collection “The Usual Suspects” on Dimple Discs on November 13, 2026. Originally released in 2017, the 23-track set has been unavailable for years and now changes hands at collectors’ prices; the digital edition is already available on Bandcamp, with the physical 2xCD prepared for that November date to coincide with a UK and Belgium tour. Usual Suspects by Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart “The Usual Suspects” gathers new recordings of Wobble’s solo material alongside songs from Invaders Of The Heart and his former band Public Image Ltd (PiL), drawn from a catalogue spanning almost forty years at the time of recording. The album was recorded at The Smokehouse studios in East London and opens with a version of PiL’s debut single “Public Image”, reworked from the band’s 1978 debut album. Other highlights include cover versions of the film themes to “Midnight Cowboy” and “Get Carter”, Dawn Penn’s “You Don’t Love Me (No, No, No)” featuring vocalist Aurora Dawn, and a new take on “Visions Of You”, which originally featured Sinéad O’Connor on Invaders Of The Heart’s Mercury Prize-nominated 1992 album “Rising Above Bedlam”. The set closes with live recordings of “Liquidator” and “Poptones”, the latter drawn from PiL’s “Metal Box”. Recording personnel on “The Usual Suspects” comprised Jah Wobble on bass, vocals and percussion, Marc Layton-Bennett on drums, percussion and backing vocals, Martin Chung on guitars, George King on keyboards and backing vocals, Steve Rigby on programming and backing vocals, Sean Corby on trumpet and flugelhorn, Aurora Dawn on vocals, and Holly Macve on vocals. Of the band behind the album, Wobble said: “This band has been a delight to play with. Similar to my first early ’80s version of the Invaders, they can all really play, plus all genre bases […] are covered. It’s a big deal to me, because it’s like a 35 year old dream has finally been realised. This is how I heard The Invaders of the Heart sound all those years ago. A classy fusion of genres. Groovy, dubby but always changing and developing. Never standing still.” Tour dates for Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart The reissue follows a UK tour and comes ahead of Belgian dates in November. Confirmed shows: October 3 – Stourbridge, Katie Fitzgerald’s (UK) October 16 – Todmorden, Unitarian Church (UK) October 21 – Frome, The Tunnels (UK) October 22 – Bristol, The Fleece (UK) October 23 – Reading, Face Bar (UK) November 7 – London, Bush Hall (UK) November 25 – Hasselt, Club AFF (Belgium) November 26 – Bruges, Cactus Muziekcentrum (Belgium) November 27 – Oudenaarde, Harmonie Oudenaarde (Belgium) Tickets are available via Songkick. About Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart Jah Wobble, born John Wardle, is a bass guitarist and vocalist from East London who was the original bassist in Public Image Ltd alongside John Lydon from the band’s 1978 formation, co-writing and playing on the 1979 album “Metal Box” before leaving in late 1980. He formed Jah Wobble’s Invaders Of The Heart in 1982, and in the early 1980s collaborated with Holger Czukay and Jaki Liebezeit of Can, as well as U2 guitarist The Edge and producer François Kevorkian. Invaders Of The Heart’s commercial peak came with 1991’s “Rising Above Bedlam”, nominated for the Mercury Prize, which included the UK top-40 single “Visions Of You” featuring Sinéad O’Connor. Wobble has since worked with artists including Ginger Baker, Björk, Brian Eno, Baaba Maal, Massive Attack, Sinéad O’Connor, Pharoah Sanders and his wife Zi Lan Liao on guzheng and harp. He reunited with former PiL guitarist Keith Levene in 2012 for the “Metal Box in Dub” shows and the album “Yin & Yang”. Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart recorded “The Usual Suspects” at The Smokehouse studios in East London, releasing it in 2017 following a six-month UK tour, as covered by Side-Line at the time. More recently, Wobble released the albums “Dub, Vol 1” (2025) and “Automated Paradise” (2026, with former Siouxsie & The Banshees guitarist Jon Klein) on Dimple Discs, and “Mystic Liverpool: The Beatles Psychedelic Songbook” with his sons, who record as Tian Qiyi, released by Cherry Red in August 2026. His autobiography, “Memoirs of a Geezer: Music, Life, Mayhem”, was published by Serpent’s Tail in 2009 and reissued in expanded form as “Dark Luminosity” by Faber & Faber in 2024. Dimple Discs now reissues “The Usual Suspects” as a 2xCD on November 13, 2026, timed to Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart’s UK and Belgium tour dates.
items._cn_summary: Jah Wobble领衔的《The Usual Suspects》2xCD再版收录了他个人作品、Invaders Of The Heart乐队曲目以及前乐队Public Image Ltd（PiL）作品的重新演绎，横跨近四十年的创作生涯。录制于伦敦东区的Smokehouse工作室，以PiL 1978年首张单曲《Public Image》开场，另有《Midnight Cowboy》《Get Carter》等电影主题曲翻唱，以及与Aurora Dawn合作的Dawn Penn名曲《You Don’t Love Me (No, No, No)》和曾与Sinéad O'Connor合作的《Visions Of You》新版，结尾收录《Liquidator》《Poptones》现场录音。Wobble本人形容这是一支跨流派融合的乐队，涵盖dub律动与多元风格变化。整体偏向dub与后朋克融合的世界音乐路线，但内容为新闻通稿形式，缺乏深度评论。

items.body: Nine Inch Nails released their third studio album, “The Fragile,” through Nothing Records and Interscope Records on 21 September 1999. The industrial rock record arrived as a double album of 23 tracks running one hour and 43 minutes, split across two discs titled “Left” and “Right.” It turns 27 this year. Five years separated “The Fragile” from “The Downward Spiral.” Trent Reznor recorded and mixed the album at Nothing Studios in New Orleans between 1997 and 1999, producing it with Alan Moulder, who also engineered and mixed. Steve Albini handled supplemental drum recording at his Electrical Audio in Chicago, Tom Baker mastered at Precision Mastering, and Bob Ezrin was credited for final continuity and flow. Dr. Dre assisted with the mix on “Even Deeper.” Danny Lohner played guitars on six tracks and contributed drum programming and synthesizers, Adrian Belew added guitar to “Just Like You Imagined,” “The Great Below” and “Where Is Everybody?”, and Mike Garson played piano on “Just Like You Imagined,” “The Way Out Is Through” and “Ripe (With Decay).” Bill Rieflin drummed on “La Mer” alongside vocalist Denise Milfort, Jerome Dillon supplied chorus drums on “We’re in This Together,” and Charlie Clouser, Keith Hillebrandt and Steve Duda covered programming and sound design. David Carson took art direction, design and photography. Disc one, “Left,” runs “Somewhat Damaged,” “The Day the World Went Away,” “The Frail,” “The Wretched,” “We’re in This Together,” “The Fragile,” “Just Like You Imagined,” “Even Deeper,” “Pilgrimage,” “No, You Don’t,” “La Mer” and “The Great Below.” Disc two, “Right,” runs “The Way Out Is Through,” “Into the Void,” “Where Is Everybody?”, “The Mark Has Been Made,” “Please,” “Starfuckers, Inc.,” “Complication,” “I’m Looking Forward to Joining You, Finally,” “The Big Come Down,” “Underneath It All” and “Ripe (With Decay).” Three singles came from the album: “The Day the World Went Away” on 20 July 1999, “We’re in This Together” on 27 September 1999 and “Into the Void” on 10 January 2000, with “Starfuckers, Inc.” issued as a promotional single. The album entered the Billboard 200 at number one with first-week sales of 229,000 copies, the band’s first chart-topping album, then fell to number 16 the following week. The RIAA certified it double platinum on 4 January 2000, and it had sold 898,000 copies in the United States by May 2005. The US edition appeared as a two-CD tri-fold digipak; the three-LP vinyl pressing carried two tracks absent from the CD, “10 Miles High” and “The New Flesh,” and came in a gatefold sleeve with a 24-page booklet. In 2017 the album was reissued on vinyl as a Definitive Edition alongside “The Fragile: Deviations 1,” a limited four-LP instrumental set that was not pressed to CD. The album streams on Spotify. Sources differ on the exact day: MusicBrainz lists 20 September 1999, while Wikipedia, Discogs and Spotify all give 21 September 1999. About Nine Inch Nails Trent Reznor formed Nine Inch Nails in Cleveland, Ohio in 1988, writing and recording the project’s material during off-hours at Right Track Studio, where he worked as an engineer and janitor. TVT Records issued the debut album, “Pretty Hate Machine,” on 20 October 1989. The “Broken” EP followed in 1992, by which point Reznor had negotiated the Nothing Records imprint through Interscope, and “The Downward Spiral” arrived in 1994. Side-Line covered the 2019 book “Into The Never”, which examined that album’s cultural reach, and reported that Johnny Cash initially resisted recording “Hurt”, the “Downward Spiral” track he covered in 2002. “The Fragile” closed the 1990s for the band, and the remix album “Things Falling Apart” followed in 2000. Reznor returned with “With Teeth” in 2005, “Year Zero” in 2007, and both “Ghosts I-IV” and “The Slip” in 2008. Atticus Ross became a full member ahead of “Hesitation Marks” in 2013, and the pair have scored film and television alongside the band since. Side-Line has since reported on Reznor’s appearance on the deluxe vinyl reissue of the 1990 Pigface debut, the Future Ruins festival announced by Reznor and Ross in 2025, the “TRON Ares: Divergence” companion album, and the “Nine Inch Noize” collaboration with Boys Noize released in April 2026. “The Fragile” turns 27 this year, the record that took the band to number one in the United States for the first time.
items._cn_summary: 本文是一篇关于九寸钉乐队1999年专辑《The Fragile》发行27周年的纪念性新闻文章，主要以信息罗列方式回顾了这张双碟专辑的制作背景与人员配置。Trent Reznor在新奥尔良Nothing Studios与Alan Moulder合作录制，Bob Ezrin负责整体连贯性把控，Steve Albini参与鼓的补充录制，还邀请了Adrian Belew、Mike Garson、Danny Lohner等客座乐手。专辑包含23首曲目，时长约一小时四十三分钟，发行于Interscope Records。文章罗列了单曲发行日期、Billboard 200首周登顶成绩及RIAA双白金认证等商业数据，但并未对音乐本身的实验性结构、声响设计或艺术价值进行实质性评论。作为一张工业摇滚标杆专辑，其制作规模和跨界合作具有一定话题性，但文章本身缺乏深度乐评视角，更接近唱片档案式的事实陈述。

items.body: From its roots as a music blog to a fiercely independent label built around physical releases, Somewherecold Records has grown from Jason Lamoreaux’s love of experimental music into a deeply personal effort to give artists and their work something lasting to hold onto. There’s (still) a chill in the air… Déka by The Corrupting Sea   When did Somewherecold Records start, and what was your inspiration? Jason Lamoreaux :: The original version of the label was a partnership with another label in Texas. I think we put out 8 or so albums with them. In 2008, the blog shut down for really accidental reasons and I wanted to start it back up again in 2016. Part of the initiative was the fact that I started to record under The Corrupting Sea and wanted to put my own music out because I thought no one else would care (I’m glad I was very wrong). Anyway, I was a shoegaze DJ at the time and ran into The Beremy Jet‘s EPs but they had no physical release. For me, digital only is a travesty for many albums. I’m very much a physical media person because the entire package is the album. I love putting artwork together, getting the right combination of packaging, and offering the world something to actually hold. Perhaps that’s the Gen Xer in me but I can’t get beyond it really. So, once The Beremy Jets was on board, I began reaching out to folks I had interviewed or reviewed or I was a fan of and brought some into the label. As of now, the roster has been whittled down extensively due to money, health issues, and just the world in general seeming to reject art (perhaps out of financial desperation or something other). At the end of the day, I just want to leave something beautiful behind in this world. The structure of the label is very much inspired by Daniel Miller and the early Mute Records approach to artists. He did it right with honor. He can sleep at night while I don’t know how other record label CEOs can (I’m speaking primarily about major labels that rip off their artists). Anyway, That’s the short of it. Who were some of your initial artist relations, and did your location help or hinder progress? Jason Lamoreaux :: I started the label while living in Texas. I hadn’t gotten to the point where I wanted to play live or even had figured out how to do so with what I was putting together. The location however was great because there are so many experimental artists in Dallas and Austin and getting to cut my teeth live in those places was a huge challenge and inspiration. I didn’t get any on the label till later for some reason, but the label was young and others had different outlets. Initial artists included Aidan Baker, Ummagma, Mis+ress, Yellow6, Niev, Zombie Girlfriend, Thee Koukouvaya, Winterwood, and then my projects like The Corrupting Sea, The Warm Jets, and more came later. I think I’ve worked with around 50 artists over the years. What were some challenges of starting the label, and how did you envision it standing apart? Jason Lamoreaux :: I’m not sure how to answer this except the Somewherecold reputation was well received in the music world because we did a lot of work on interviews and reviews between 2000-2008. I initially started the blog up again with interviews from God is an Astronaut and The Album Leaf but the label side of things started to overwhelm and I decided to move in that direction for the time being. The label is curated by me and I guess that’s the thread through the label. Walls of sound, intimate ambience, electronic experimental, cowboy drone, and other genres are, for me, deeply connected and I wanted the label to reflect my love for those things. Further, I’m an artist. I wanted to be an artist available to other artists. It felt like purpose and, in many ways, still does. What is your motivation in keeping the label moving forward into the next decade? Jason Lamoreaux :: This is a constant question in the back of my mind. I would love for it take off and people to actually support it in full. We don’t press very many physical copies but the current landscape makes it almost impossible to sell out it seems. There is a lot of noise out there, too many algorithms, and a ton of cynicism. So, in my mind, I’m taking it year by year. Once it becomes too onerous, I will likely walk away and maybe keep me and a few collective artists to keep it going. But, for now, we stay the course. That said, Elasticstage in the UK has made it possible to release so much music on vinyl and CDs over on the European side of things. My first 10 The Corrupting Sea albums are now up for order there as well as all the new releases for the label. It’s a press on demand site and the products are beautiful and sound great. The shipping is very low if you order 3 items (their limite right now per order) at a time. “There is a lot of noise out there, too many algorithms, and a ton of cynicism. So, in my mind, I’m taking it year by year.” ~Jason Lamoureaux How do you deliver the label’s “sound” to listeners and fans (through distribution, campaigns, live shows, word of mouth, etc.)? Jason Lamoreaux :: There are a number of ways. I have a rather large promo email system but that is also an issue since so many get inundated with requests for review, etc (I know you probably get the same). The label does have distribution through The Business in Anacortes, Washington. The place is run by this amazing couple and I wish folks would use them more. Again, getting above the noise as it were. Most of my artists play live but I don’t see that as a deal breaker. A Journey of Giraffes is a studio project and has been so well received. Others are new and I’m not sure if they will play live or not. Again, not a deal breaker. I think people can enjoy music outside of the live world especially considering how terrible support for local artists has become in those live spaces. In terms of word of mouth, well, the silence can be deafening. As a label owner, you often have no idea what fans are thinking, if the label is being well received, or artists being listened to until you bump into someone who tells you differently. You would think that with the mountain of communication options, you would hear things. But you don’t and it can get quite lonely. I do post on social media but I’m beginning to see it as a hindrance rather than a plus. The label is heavily pro-lgbtq+, anti-war, pro-immigrants, and more. The people who run these sites have proven to be otherwise and it’s becoming more and more difficult to justify any presence on Social Media. At this moment, plans are being sorted to go to a singular website with Bandcamp attached and nothing more. Lastly, I have uploaded to streaming, which, financially, is a joke. Does it capture people’s attention? I have no idea. You have to have so many streams even to make a penny. I’m behind on those uploads but the label is in a moment of organization and I’ll be uploading past albums that I’ve missed due to daily life. For me, streaming is not a priority. For the same reasons I dislike social media, I dislike streaming companies even more. Spotify, for me, is now a no go. I refuse to place my own music up there but my other artists are welcome to on their own. I don’t control their music. The Déka box set is encased in a purple velvet box set. It contains the first 10 albums remastered by Jason T. Lamoreaux. All come in artwork matching the box. Also, each album except for Ontology has a brand new track attached as a hidden track. Visit Somewherecold Records: Bandcamp | Somewherecold.net Déka by The Corrupting Sea The post Five questions with Somewherecold Records first appeared on Igloo Magazine.

items.body: Review by Progfan97402 — I have both 1970s Sebastian Hardie albums and Symphinity from Windchase (which was Mario Millo andToivo Pilt with new guys) and I'll have to say Windchase (the album) is my least favorite of thethree. It's clear the inspiration has slipped. This out of the way: "Love, Life and Music" is rathersappy and easily the worst thing on the album. The title track is not on the level of Four Momentsbut has done nice passages but parts of it bore me. For me "Hello Phimistar" is the best thing onthe album. For some reason Toivo Pilt decides to cut back on the Mellotron in favor of the stringsynths. While I wasn't big on Four Moments it definitely had better compositions. For me I muchprefer the Windchase album that was to appear the next year, it's actually quite underrated.Windchase (the album) clearly shows their hearts weren't always there. Has its moments but,strangely Symphinity is my favorite of the three.
items._cn_summary: 这张1976年的交响前卫摇滚专辑是澳大利亚乐队Sebastian Hardie解散后由核心成员Mario Millo与Toivo Pilt组建的Windchase项目的首张作品。乐评指出专辑整体灵感已不如前作，其中《Love, Life and Music》被评价为专辑中最弱的一曲，略显感伤；《Hello Phimistar》则是全专辑最出色的曲目。制作上乐队减少了Mellotron的使用，转而以弦乐合成器为主要音色，这在一定程度上影响了专辑的氛围与厚度。整体而言，乐评认为乐队在这张作品中投入的情感有所下滑，尽管下一年的同名专辑被认为更为出色且被严重低估，但首张专辑仍暴露出创作动力不足的问题。
