items.body: Review by Prog Dog — This is actually a divisive album among devoted Yes fans, mainly because of the absence of key founding member and vocalist Jon Anderson. Gone was his distinct and immediately recognizable high tenor voice, along with the more fanciful and fantasy-like lyrics that had become part of the Yes sound. For others, it may be the departure of keyboardist Rick Wakeman that makes Drama difficult to embrace. Filling his shoes was Geoff Downes, whose keyboard approach was quite different from Wakeman's. Although Downes had considerable classical training, his work on Drama placed greater emphasis on texture, tone and the emerging possibilities of synthesizers and electronic technology, bringing some of the new-wave sensibilities of the Buggles into Yes.I recall that sometime around 1980, or perhaps early 1981, my brother and I had each picked up another Yes album. I got Tormato; he got Drama. Neither of us, as very new Yes fans at the time, realized that Jon Anderson wasn't on Drama. Instead, Trevor Horn, known for his work with the Buggles, had stepped into Anderson's shoes.My brother asked if I wanted to trade. I don't remember whether I agreed or not'I liked both albums equally. If I had based the trade strictly on the album artwork, though, Drama would have won hands down. It's one of Roger Dean's great Yes covers.One of the great tracks on this important album is the opening epic 'Machine Messiah.' For anyone who had become a fan of Steve Howe's guitar work and direction on Tormato, this must have been something of a shock. As the track begins Howe goes all-in on the heavy, riff-driven guitar sound here, venturing into territory that sounds like an early precursor to prog-metal. Not that he hadn't demonstrated an aggressive side before, with tracks such as 'The Gates of Delirium,' 'Close to the Edge,' 'Heart of the Sunrise,' and 'Perpetual Change.' But this was different'a heavier, more metallic approach that, in retrospect, foreshadowed the emergence of that off-shoot of prog-rock.The track changes its palette several times, at one point featuring tentative acoustic guitar and an epic, almost devotional or cultish atmosphere as technology is worshipped and revered. It feels surprisingly prescient today. Another major section is full of hope, though, as Horn reaches for notes his vocal cords could barely have been expected to reach: 'Maybe we'll change / Offered the chance / To finally unlearn our lessons and alter our stance.' 'Man in a White Car' is a little ditty that I wish they had developed into a full-grown song. Instead, it serves nicely as a palette cleanser after the frighteningly epic 'Machine Messiah,' which sounds like it could easily have drawn lightning bolts down from the sky.'Does It Really Happen' features one of Chris Squire's all-time hookiest bass lines. Alan White's sheer power and focus as a drummer is especially potent throughout this album, on this track as on any on Drama. The drums and bass feed off each other with near-ferocity, while the vocals are equally aggressive. Squire's distinctive voice shines through on this one, while Horn's singing is also well showcased. Together, they form something of a power duo.The new-wave vibes are prominent in the opening melodic instrumental section, but there are hints of Yes' Going for the One too, thanks to Steve Howe's distorted pedal steel, with his steel bar swooping between the chords.'Into the Lens' is the oft-overshadowed track on this album, despite showcasing the band's hyper-creativity. Horn provides some more emotional and introspective vocals, with lyrics that seem to explore detachment and observation. Once again, Downes' synths transport Yes firmly into new-wave territory, while the song still holds onto its proggy identity through its numerous passages and sections. There's even a wonderfully eclectic mix of sounds, including sitar and vocoder. Howe also leans into his 'talking guitar' sound, using a wah-wah pedal to make the instrument seem to speak.'Run Through the Light' is a rare and daring track for Yes, featuring Trevor Horn on fretless bass while Squire instead plays some affected piano chords around the track. Horn's vocals add a completely new sound for Yes, with a staccato, almost stuttering effect. It seems likely Squire was coaching Horn through the track, and there's a story that by having Horn play bass, the song was more likely to make the final album cut'something Squire seemed quite determined to ensure.'Tempus Fugit' is a muscular song. Chris Squire provides the fast, heavy bass riffs that hold the whole thing together like the bones of a roller coaster. There's also some early use of the Fairlight CMI in the 'yes, yes, yes, yes' synthetic vocal samples at the end. It's an amusing little break in the fourth wall, with Yes seemingly making a self-conscious reference to itself. I can attest to how effective it was: my first conscious exposure to Yes was hearing this song on the radio, and that repeated 'yes, yes, yes, yes' stuck in my head. After running downstairs to tell my brother about this new band I had discovered, I would soon be buying my first Yes records. Ironically, Drama was one of the last Yes albums my brother and I actually bought in around 1980. This is not Yes's best record, but it is essential nonetheless, chock full of exciting music, and everyone in the band sounds fresh and revitalized. I give it a 4.75 out of 5 dog bones. (5 for prog archives round-ed off score)

items._cn_summary: 该专辑是Yes乐队1980年的转型之作，在主唱Jon Anderson和键盘手Rick Wakeman离队后，由Buggles乐队的Trevor Horn和Geoff Downes加入填补。Downes的键盘手法偏向合成器音色与新潮质感，与Wakeman的古典化风格形成鲜明对比。Steve Howe在开场曲'Machine Messiah'中展示了更重、更金属化的吉他riff，被视为前卫金属的早期雏形。曲目中段穿插原声段落，营造出近乎宗教崇拜般的氛围，主题围绕科技崇拜展开，具有一定的前瞻性。Horn的人声在某些高音段落展现出令人惊讶的力度。整张专辑在Yes经典旋律性与新潮合成器质感之间寻求平衡，虽有创新尝试，但更接近主流前卫摇滚框架内的调整，对追求实验性、前卫融合与极端创新听感的听众而言，跨界幅度有限。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — One could understand and appreciate this Muse album only by knowing that the band had attempted tocreate something completely out of the ordinary even by their own standards. An album that has Queenand Skrillex as major influences is meant to be compositionally intense and stylistically chaotic,which is precisely what 'The 2nd Law' is - a collection of epic, theatrical, and electronic-riddenpop rock anthems that broadly explore the concepts of authoritarianism, power-control dynamics aswell as conspiracy and fiction. A fascinating mixture of disparate styles is at stake here, as theband offers an entertaining collection informed by past releases like 'The Resistance', but leaningmore into the artsy electronic side of their music. However, with its thirteen tracks, 'The 2nd Law'is hardly the most consistent release from the British trio. The futuristic production stylehighlights the strong melodies on tracks like 'Animals' and 'Save Me', but it also renders some ofthe mellower songs utterly dull.The stark contrasts between the funky dance pop elements, the hammering rock riffs, the energeticdubstep beats, and the operatic vocal experiments, however, make 'The 2nd Law' somewhat of aschizophrenic listen. This is effective and engaging for a while, especially when the listener ispresented with excellent songs like the Bond movie theme opener 'Supremacy', the electro-poppysingle 'Madness', or the funk rock number 'Panic Station' in the very beginning of the record, butthe effect soon washes away as certain songs begin to resemble Radiohead or Queen way too blatantly.The two Chris Wolstenholme features are quite good, nevertheless, with 'Liquid State' being animportant album highlight, in my opinion, depicting the band's bass player as a strong vocalists andsongwriter. The two closing pieces are quite interesting as well, despite being mostly instrumentaland vastly dubstep-inspired. I still think the use of electronics and digital instruments on thisalbum is one of its stronger features, but the overall mixture of genres and dynamics can easilybecome overwhelming. I would not call 'The 2nd Law' a classic but I definitely feel it is the kindof record only Muse could attempt to produce.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑试图在Muse自身标准之外进行大胆实验，融合Queen式的戏剧化编排与Skrillex启发的电子制作，形成歌剧式人声、放克舞曲、猛烈摇滚riff与dubstep节拍并存的拼贴格局。专辑探讨威权主义与阴谋虚构等主题，制作上偏向未来感的电子化处理，使《Animals》《Save Me》等旋律强劲曲目突出，但部分柔和曲目因过度电子化而显得乏味。开场几首作品如《Supremacy》《Madness》《Panic Station》呈现强烈吸引力，但后续曲目对Radiohead和Queen的模仿痕迹过于明显。贝斯手Chris Wolstenholme主唱的两首作品成为亮点，结尾两首纯器乐dubstep曲目也颇具趣味。整体风格杂糅且动态起伏大，虽具Muse独特色彩，但在一致性与深度上有所欠缺，更接近主流流行摇滚的范畴。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: Sean Cooney 这张专辑以1819年英国彼得卢屠杀为题材，通过原创歌曲重新审视这一工人阶级历史事件。专辑以书籍形式呈现，辅以历史信件、政治漫画和插图，构成多媒体项目。合作阵容包括吉他手Sam Carter、小提琴手兼歌手Eliza Carthy、多乐器演奏者Ben Nicholls以及兰开夏工业民谣歌手Jennifer Reid，后者在叙事部分也有贡献。歌曲捕捉了集会当日的氛围——从期盼与兴奋到骑兵冲散人群的恐怖，再到事后的悲恸。Cooney 的创作聚焦于个人叙事，通过小人物的视角展开历史画面。作为工人阶级历史的音乐记录，这张专辑在当下抗议空间收紧的语境下具有现实意义，但整体仍属传统民谣范畴，音乐风格较为保守，缺乏实验性元素，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、电子及融合风格差距较大。

items.body: The chorus of “Don’t Try” turns an old piece of street wisdom into a hook: “Don’t try piss on me and tell me it’s raining”. The man it is aimed at takes the credit for work he did not do, hands out promises that come to nothing, expects the overtime as standard and treats one late morning as an offence. Past him stand all the others: the smile that turns into a betrayal, the boasting about how easily things arrive, the liberties taken without a second thought. The last verse hands the accusation back, on the old line about the three fingers that point home whenever one goes out. Messenjah open Social Commentary with it, seven tracks of reggae made with The Aarons Brothers and released on Reload Records in April 2025. They have played roots reggae since forming in Kitchener, Ontario in 1981, and became the first Canadian reggae band signed to a major label when Warner Music Canada took Rock You High and put the music on national radio here for the first time. That was the second door Rupert “Ojiji” Harvey had opened, after Crack of Dawn, the Toronto soul group he co-founded, became the first Black Canadian band to sign a major deal. He has led Messenjah since the mid-1980s, through Reggae Sunsplash in Montego Bay, a Juno for Catch De Vibe, and a night in 1998 playing for Nelson Mandela at Toronto’s SkyDome. Hear “Don’t Try” HERE and pick up Social Commentary through THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Messenjah & The Aarons Brothers – Don’t Try appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: Messenjah 与 The Aarons Brothers 合作推出的专辑《Social Commentary》收录七首雷鬼作品，以《Don't Try》开篇，歌词直面职场与社交中的虚伪与背叛。主唱 Rupert "Ojiji" Harvey 自1981年起在加拿大安大略省基奇纳活跃，曾与华纳音乐加拿大签约，是加拿大雷鬼乐坛的重要人物。乐队历经多年舞台历练，包括蒙特哥贝 Reggae Sunsplash 音乐节、多伦多 SkyDome 为曼德拉演出等。整体风格延续传统根源雷鬼路线，歌词承载社会批判意识，专辑由 Reload Records 于2025年4月发行。文章以新闻推介形式介绍作品及乐队历史背景，缺乏对音乐制作、编曲细节或声音设计方面的深入评析。

items.body: Clan of Xymox, the Dutch darkwave and gothic rock project led by Ronny Moorings, released “Notes From The Underground” on 21 September 2001 through Pandaimonium Records in Europe. The album turns 25 this year. Metropolis Records issued it in North America nine days later, on 30 September 2001. Moorings wrote, recorded and mixed all twelve tracks, and produced the record with Mojca Zugna. It was the third studio album of the reformed Clan of Xymox era, after “Hidden Faces” from 1997 and “Creatures” from 1999. Three of its songs were already in circulation by the time it appeared. The “Liberty” CD single, issued by Pandaimonium on 20 October 2000 alongside the band’s double live album, carried “Liberty” together with “Number One” and “At Your Mercy”. Clan of Xymox’s ‘Notes From The Underground’ tracklist and credits The CD runs twelve tracks: “Innocent”, “I Want You Now”, “Internal Darkness”, “At Your Mercy”, “Anguish”, “Number One”, “Into Her Web”, “The Bitter Sweet”, “Liberty”, “Something Wrong”, “Mysterium” and “The Same Dream”. Dierk Budde mastered the album and Mojca Zugna made the sleeve artwork. The band’s official biography states the record reached number 2 on the German DAC chart and topped the US Musicfolio poll for 2001. The same page quotes a Side-Line review of the album as reading “This album is to be seen as a milestone in the band’s discography towards which their previous efforts all converge, or emerge from.” Pandaimonium returned to the material in May 2002 with “Remixes From The Underground”, a two-disc set that reworked every song on the album. Its contributors included Front 242, Assemblage 23, In Strict Confidence, Iris, Angels & Agony and Beborn Beton, and the limited edition added the band’s first video disc. Notes from the Underground by Clan Of Xymox About Clan of Xymox Ronny Moorings formed the band in 1981 in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. Its first release, the mini-album “Subsequent Pleasures”, appeared in 1983 in a run of 500 copies recorded on a four-track home setup. Demo material sent with it led to a deal with 4AD, and the self-titled album followed in 1985, cut at Palladium Studios in Edinburgh and co-produced with label head Ivo Watts-Russell. “Medusa” came next on the same label, and the band contributed “Muscoviet Musquito” to the 4AD compilation “Lonely Is An Eyesore” in 1987. The group parted with 4AD in October 1988, signed to Wing, a PolyGram subsidiary, and shortened its name to Xymox. “Twist of Shadows” arrived in 1989 with the singles “Obsession”, “Imagination” and “Blind Hearts”; the band’s official biography puts its sales above 300,000 copies. “Phoenix” followed in 1991 and closed the Wing chapter when PolyGram wound the label down. “Metamorphosis” and “Headclouds” then came out on the UK independent Zok Records. Moorings also wrote music for two CD-ROM games in the same period, “Total Mayhem” in 1996 and “Revenant” a year later. In 1997 Moorings ended the Xymox era, restarted the band as Clan of Xymox and signed to Tess Records. “Hidden Faces” appeared that year, produced by Dave M. Allen and John A. Rivers. “Creatures” followed in 1999, mixed by Rivers and Moorings, and moved the band to Metropolis Records in North America and Pandaimonium Records in Europe, the pairing that would also handle “Notes From The Underground”. The double live album “LIVE”, drawn from the band’s South and Central American shows, came out in October 2000. “Farewell” arrived in 2003, and “The Best Of Clan Of Xymox”, with its running order chosen by a fan poll, in September 2004. The “Weak In My Knees” EP opened 2006 ahead of the album “Breaking Point”. In early 2009 the band moved to Trisol Records in Europe while staying with Metropolis in the United States, and “In Love We Trust” came out on 18 August 2009, covered in Clan of Xymox’s ‘In Love We Trust’ turns 17 on 18 August. The thirteenth studio album “Darkest Hour” followed on 20 May 2011, the covers set “Kindred Spirits” in October 2012 and “Matters Of Mind, Body And Soul” on 14 February 2014. “Days Of Black” arrived on 7 April 2017, reported in Clan Of Xymox return with new album: ‘Days Of Black’. “Spider On The Wall” followed in 2020, announced in New Clan Of Xymox album ‘Spider On The Wall’ and video for ‘All I Ever Know’, and Moorings talked through his writing that September in Interview with Clan Of Xymox: ‘For Me A Lot Of These Memories Are Finished Stories Without A Soundtrack’. “Limbo”, written during the pandemic lockdowns, arrived in July 2021 and was previewed in Clan Of Xymox returns with all new album ‘Limbo’ in July. The eighteenth album “Exodus” followed in June 2024, reported in Clan Of Xymox announce new album for June: ‘Exodus’, with the “Blood of Christ” EP later that year and a 3CD edition of “Exodus” in February 2025. Moorings looked back across the full run in Ronny Moorings (Clan Of Xymox), an exclusive retrospective interview. Moorings has been the only constant member and still writes, records and produces the band’s music. The live line-up is Moorings on vocals, guitar and melodica, Mojca Zugna on bass, Mario Usai on guitar and bass, and Sean Winzer on keyboards, synth drums and backing vocals. Twenty-five years on, “Notes From The Underground” sits between “Creatures” and “Farewell” in that sequence.
items._cn_summary: 该文章并非传统意义上的乐评，而是Side-Line为Clan of Xymox 2001年专辑《Notes From The Underground》发行25周年所撰写的纪念性新闻稿。内容以专辑基本信息为主，包括发行日期（2001年9月21日由Pandaimonium在欧洲发行，Metropolis在北美发行）、曲目列表、录制人员、厂牌背景及乐队历史回顾。文章提及该专辑曾在德国DAC榜达到第2位、获得2001年Musicfolio评选榜首，并引用了一段官方传记中的评语。此外还介绍了2002年的混音合辑《Remixes From The Underground》，参与混音的包括Front 242、Assemblage 23、In Strict Confidence等电子工业艺人。文章本身缺乏对音乐本身的声音分析、创作手法或艺术价值的深入评述，信息密度低，更接近档案性资料整理。

items.body:
A new concert spotlighting trans, non-binary, and gender non-conforming artists is coming to Singapore.

The inaugural T4T4T4T show will take place on 6 October at Room 526, bringing together RENE, Marian Carmel, haldi honey, and Australia's FVNERAL for a night of live music and community.

Announced by Singapore independent artist RENE, the concert is billed as the first of its kind in the country.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by RENE (@reneannwong)

“We're so excited to bring this show to life,” shared RENE. “It's rare to see diverse and queer identities celebrated on stage in Singapore, so we're doing this to bring our community together for a night of great music.”

They added: “We hope this show might also inspire the organisation of more shows that platform trans, non-binary, and gender non-conforming artists, it would be amazing if we can do a T4T4T4T part 2! And so on!”

The lineup spans indie rock, math-pop, indie-pop, and more. Australian indie rock outfit FVNERAL is the brainchild of trans non-binary songwriter and producer Tay Blunt, who is also the founder and director of TRANSGENRE, Australia's first festival with an entirely trans lineup.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by RENE (@reneannwong)

Singapore math-pop band haldi honey, founded by Daxa, will also take the stage, alongside Philippines-born, Singapore-based singer-songwriter and visual artist Marian Carmel. Rounding out the lineup is RENE, whose sound draws from pop, indie, and rock.

Beyond the music, T4T4T4T will also give back to the community. Ten per cent of ticket proceeds will go to TransBefrienders, a local charity providing accessible health and social support to transgender and gender-diverse individuals.

Purchase tickets here.

Like what you read? Show our writer some love!

items.body:
CLOSE YOUR EYES are kicking off their next chapter with 'Open Your Eyes'.

Released on 18 September, the pre-release single serves as the first taste of the seven-member K-pop group's upcoming fourth mini album, 256th Note. It follows their third mini album, blackout, which arrived in November 2025.

'Open Your Eyes' brings together jazz, hip-hop and R&B, pairing an experimental piano arpeggio loop with fast-paced drums. The track also features pianist Yohan Kim and jazz saxophonist Jacob Scesney, whose performances add to its jazz-influenced sound.

The release continues CLOSE YOUR EYES' musical evolution following their debut with first mini album ETERNALT in April 2025. Formed through reality competition PROJECT7, the group comprises JEON MINWOOK, MA JINGXIANG, JANG YEOJUN, KIM SUNGMIN, SONG SEUNGHO, KENSHIN, and SEO KYOUNGBAE.

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — *Here Comes the Rain* is most likely the final album by Magnum, a British hard rock band formed in 1972, with 25 studio albums to its credit if you count the two albums released in 1997 and 1999 under the name Hard Rain. With about ten tracks per album, that brings the total to around 250 songs, almost all of which were composed by guitarist Tony Clarkin (he only let Russ Ballard help him with a few minor tracks on the 1990 album *Goodnight L.A.*). This simple calculation highlights just how prolific a songwriter Clarkin was?a rarity in this field. I wrote "was" because Tony suddenly passed away in early January 2024, four days before the release of this quasi-posthumous album.Beyond the context of this tragic event, dedicating a few lines to Magnum in a French magazine devoted to progressive music?even in the broadest sense?is debatable. It's true that aside from the first two albums, *Kingdom of Madness* (1978) and *Magnum II* (1979)?to which one might possibly add the less simplistic half of *The Eleventh Hour* (1983) and *On a Storyteller's Night* (1985)? four highly recommended albums in which the British band seemed to put their own spin on the American formula for full-bodied pop-prog that Styx and Boston had devised with the success we all know, the rest of Magnum's discography offered nothing more than yet another high-energy AOR album.Carefully crafted melodies, a rigid structure that very often followed the verse/chorus/verse/bridge/chorus pattern, and tight, driving rhythms?all of this was far from enough for an audience seeking progressive musical brilliance, despite the regular inclusion on each album of one or two more adventurous tracks with slightly more complex structures.Since the arrival of keyboardist Rick Benton in 2018 (replacing Mark Stanway), Magnum had infused its epic stadium rock with more and more symphonic elements, leaning more often toward the sound of an energized Asia, which made each release more interesting. With its rich sound, finely crafted and catchy melodies, and flawless performance, Magnum came closer than ever to a sophisticated and universal form of heavy prog, quite close to the best of Uriah Heep, another intrepid English veteran. The ambitious *The Serpent Rings* (2020) is a good example of this."Here Comes the Rain" is cut from the same cloth. At first glance, the opening track "Run Into the Shadows," with its unstoppable riff and luminous melody, doesn't seem to represent a major musical shift. Yet hidden deep within this binary music lies a sort of irrepressible despair, a discreet melancholy. And these lyrics, chanted in a thunderous voice, describe our violent world with such darkness that it all seeps into the flashy metal on the surface. This feeling is amply confirmed by the next track, the haunting "Here Comes the Rain," with an even more progressive sound. And what can be said about "Some Kind of Treachery," a heart-wrenching waltz blending symphonic strings and romantic piano?Tony Clarkin once again wrote and composed the entire album but allowed Benton to bring more diversity and boldness to the arrangements (a Hammond organ solo on the boogie-prog track "Bleu Tango," a Moog solo on "Borderline," or classical organ arpeggios on "I Wanna Live," harp-synth sound on "Broken City," and a rhythm-and-blues brass section on "The Seventh Darkness"). Keyboards take center stage ("After the Silence," "Broken City"), while the guitars often remain in the background or provide rhythmic accompaniment, sometimes acoustic ("Here Comes the Rain," "Broken City"). This trend, combined with a greater proportion of slow, melancholic tracks with highly evocative titles (the tragic "Broken City," the anxious "Here Comes the Rain"), and more necessarily binary ones ("Some Kind of Treachery"), where singer Bob Catley?a longtime member of the band whose powerful vocals remain undiminished despite his 76 years?also knows how to be more delicate and moving?all of this makes this dark album more endearing than its predecessors.How can one remain unmoved while listening to "I Wanna Live," with its premonitory undertones, sung with rage by Catley and written by the man who would soon leave this life? I wanna live/ I wanna shout (?) / I wanna live my one desire / Come on and take my hand and walk me through the fire. The magnificent "Borderline," which evokes Rainbow, or even Fish, with its electro-tribal intro and its coda featuring delicate classical piano, brings the flawless *Here Comes the Rain* to a regal close?a bitter and pessimistic swan song, yet one devoid of weakness or clumsiness throughout these fifty memorable minutes.Magnum enjoyed little success in France but great success among our German neighbors, where the majority of their releases reached the top 5 on the sales charts. *Here Comes the Rain* even peaked at No. 2 there upon its release. It is well deserved. After a prolific career, spent largely in the service of a band he could be proud of, Tony Clarkin thus bowed out with what will certainly remain one of Magnum's best albums?an important band worth discovering if you haven't already.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是英国老牌硬摇滚乐队Magnum的疑似遗作，由核心创作者、吉他手Tony Clarkin（2024年初去世）几乎包揽全部作曲。乐评梳理了乐队跨越四十余年的创作脉络：从早期受Styx与Boston影响的流行前卫阶段，到2018年键盘手Rick Benton加入后逐渐增加交响化元素，趋近Asia与Uriah Heep那种饱满的重型前卫风格。本作延续这一路线，保留强劲riff和朗朗上口的旋律外壳，却在歌词中注入对当下世界暴力与阴暗的隐喻。'Here Comes the Rain'与'Run Into the Shadows'展现出更强的前卫气质，'Some Kind of Treachery'则以交响化华尔兹呈现悲怆情绪。整体仍属旋律驱动、结构工整的主流硬摇滚范式，与其偏好的实验与前卫路线差距明显。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由三位多伦多音乐人通过多年邮件协作完成，呈现十八首短小的简约民谣作品，总时长仅三十四分钟。编曲以原声吉他、尤克里里琴和键盘为主，配以滑动吉他和脆弱的人声，歌词围绕失去与宿命展开。专辑跨越布鲁斯、乡村灵魂乐等风格，偶尔显露更宏大的编曲意图。整体氛围被描述为梦境般的音乐，质感轻盈却饱含情感。虽然融合了多种背景音乐人的创作痕迹，但作品本质上属于精致的小型民谣创作，与实验、前卫或电子领域几乎无关，对于追求前沿声响的听众而言缺乏吸引力。
